items.title: Nvidia’s Board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang as second extra-marital affair emerges
items.description: Nvidia Board reportedly moves to expel Jensen Huang as stock tumbles on latest scandals and lack of succession plans at Nvidia.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia's Board of Directors is preparing to oust co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang following revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence and another with an Nvidia executive, reports The Wall Street Journal. Although no final decision has been made yet, the company's directors could meet as early as November 11 to discuss Huang's future. Whoever succeeds Huang will be the company's second CEO in 33 years. Nvidia's stock dropped 8% in after-hours trading following the reports. Nvidia's board of directors launched an independent investigation into the matter on November 8.The report from the WSJ comes hours after the New York Times revealed that Huang allegedly had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. According to five people who worked at Nvidia, the relationship was known internally, while Huang and Powell were reportedly seen together at a San Jose hotel during Nvidia's GTC conference in March. The allegations follow an earlier report that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese intelligence asset.A similar controversy cost Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich his position in June 2018, when an internal investigation confirmed that he had maintained a consensual relationship with an employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers. It is noteworthy that Nvidia's code of conduct explicitly identifies personal relationships as potential conflicts of interest and instructs employees to consult the company's legal department when such conflicts arise. Whether Huang violated Nvidia's internal policies remains unclear, as the code of conduct does not explicitly prohibit all relationships between managers and subordinates.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Huang's potential departure would mark the first CEO transition in Nvidia's 33-year history, and therefore his succession has become an immediate concern for Nvidia, which does not have anyone of Huang's caliber in the leadership team. Although chief financial officer Colette Kress could potentially serve as interim chief executive if Huang is ousted while the BoD searches for a permanent replacement, it remains to be seen how Wall Street would react to this assignment.Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky, who used to be the company's senior vice president of engineering and operations and remains a member of the company's board and an Nvidia Fellow, could also play a role in the succession process, given his extensive knowledge of Nvidia's technology, corporate culture, and history. However, has not served in an executive role at Nvidia for at least a decade, so the chances that he will succeed Huang are low. items.titleZh: 英伟达董事会据报准备罢免CEO黄仁勋，第二段婚外情曝光
items.descriptionZh:
据Tom's Hardware报道，英伟达董事会正筹备罢免联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋（Jensen Huang），起因是《华尔街日报》披露其存在两段婚外情：一段涉及一名被怀疑为中国情报机构工作的女性，另一段涉及英伟达内部一名直接向他汇报的高管。董事会尚未作出最终决定，但最早可能于11月11日召开会议讨论黄仁勋的去留。若黄仁勋离任，继任者将成为英伟达33年历史上第二位CEO。消息传出后，英伟达股价在盘后交易中下跌8%。董事会已于11月8日就此启动独立调查。

在《华尔街日报》报道前数小时，《纽约时报》称黄仁勋与英伟达医疗健康业务副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔（Kimberly Powell）存在婚外情，鲍威尔直接向黄仁勋汇报。五名曾在英伟达工作的知情人士称，这段关系在公司内部广为人知；据称今年3月英伟达GTC大会期间，两人曾在圣何塞一家酒店一同出现。此前还有报道称，黄仁勋与一名叫Alice Huang的华裔女商人存在关系，美国情报部门认为此人是中国情报资产。

这一风波与英特尔前CEO布莱恩·科再奇（Brian Krzanich）2018年6月的遭遇相似：当时英特尔内部调查确认科再奇与一名员工保持双方自愿的恋爱关系，违反了适用于所有管理者的禁止亲密关系政策，科再奇因此辞职。值得注意的是，英伟达的行为准则明确将私人关系列为潜在利益冲突，并指示员工在出现此类冲突时咨询公司法务部门。但由于准则并未明确禁止管理者与下属之间的一切恋爱关系，黄仁勋是否违反英伟达内部政策目前仍不清楚。

黄仁勋可能的离任将标志英伟达33年来首次CEO更替，继任问题因此成为公司当务之急，而英伟达领导团队中并无与黄仁勋同等量级的人物。若黄仁勋被罢免，首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）可能在董事会寻找正式继任者期间出任临时CEO，但华尔街对这一安排的反映尚待观察。英伟达联合创始人克里斯·马拉科夫斯基（Chris Malachowsky）也可能在继任过程中发挥作用——他曾任公司工程与运营高级副总裁，目前仍是董事会成员和英伟达院士（Nvidia Fellow），对公司的技术、企业文化和历史有深入了解；但他已至少十年未在英伟达担任高管职务，因此接替黄仁勋的可能性较低。此前周日，董事们曾对黄仁勋及其领导团队表达信心，但这一措辞并不足以保证其继续留任。

整体来看，此事的核心影响集中在公司治理与领导层稳定性层面：一方面，英伟达的行为准则与英特尔此前的处理先例，为董事会评估高管私人关系是否构成利益冲突提供了参照；另一方面，由于黄仁勋长期是英伟达战略与技术路线的核心人物，其去留的不确定性可能波及投资者信心、公司战略延续性以及华尔街对英伟达管理层的评估。

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Verge.RelatedThe US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown itThe future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life?Huang and Powell, who are both married to other people, were allegedly captured together at a hotel in San Jose during Nvidia’s GTC developer conference in March, two unnamed sources told the Times. items.titleZh: 据报道英伟达正准备解雇黄仁勋
items.descriptionZh:
据《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达董事会正准备罢免CEO黄仁勋。此前《纽约时报》称，黄仁勋被指涉及第二段婚外情；而就在几天前，他才承认与一名据称是中国间谍的女性、Megaspeed高管Alice Huang存在婚外关系。报道称，第二段涉嫌婚外情的对象是直接向黄仁勋汇报的英伟达医疗保健业务副总裁Kimberly Powell。《华尔街日报》称，英伟达董事会最快将于今天开会，决定黄仁勋在公司内的去留。英伟达未立即回应The Verge的置评请求。

《纽约时报》援引两名匿名消息人士称，黄仁勋与Powell均已婚，二人据称于今年3月英伟达GTC开发者大会期间在圣何塞一家酒店被拍到一起；但《纽约时报》表示尚未看到相关视频。CNBC援引一名匿名消息人士称，有关两人关系的传闻在英伟达内部已流传很久，部分原因是Powell没有医疗健康或科学背景。受消息影响，英伟达股价周三盘后下跌超过7%。

背景方面，英伟达和黄仁勋在周末确认了与Megaspeed高管、据称间谍Alice Huang的婚外关系，并启动后续调查。公司表示已聘请前美国联邦检察官Joon H. Kim及其所在的Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz律所处理此事。但最新传闻显示，董事会可能不会等待调查结果就采取行动。Wired报道称，黄仁勋去年还聘请了以处理公开性丑闻著称的危机公关公司Heller；该公司创始人曾为面临公众审视的多位权势人物提供建议，包括前国会议员Anthony Weiner和作家Jeffrey Toobin。Heller未立即回应The Verge的置评请求。

这篇新闻本身不涉及英伟达芯片技术发布或性能参数，核心是公司治理、高管风险和领导层不确定性。英伟达当前在AI加速芯片市场占据主导地位，其GPU和CUDA生态是全球AI训练与推理基础设施的关键。若CEO突然更迭，市场关注点将集中在董事会决策的合法性、继任安排、战略连续性以及对Blackwell等下一代AI芯片路线、客户关系和供应链的影响。盘后7%以上的跌幅已反映投资者对治理风险的即时担忧。不过，相关婚外情和“间谍”指控目前均来自媒体报道和匿名消息人士，部分内容仍有待证实；英伟达董事会最终是否罢免黄仁勋，以及调查结果如何，仍需后续确认。

items.titleZh: Jensen Huang now accused of affair with Nvidia executive who reported to him, alleged cover-up attempt — new indiscretion comes in wake of admitted affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.descriptionZh:
据《纽约时报》援引五名匿名的英伟达内部人士报道，英伟达CEO黄仁勋除此前已承认的与Alice Huang的婚外情外，还与公司直接下属、医疗健康业务副总裁Kimberly Powell存在另一段关系。报道称，今年3月英伟达在加州圣何塞举行GTC大会期间，黄仁勋与Powell被拍到在酒店内有亲密举动；拍摄者被黄仁勋安保团队带离，并被要求签署保密协议。Powell于2008年加入英伟达，此后持续晋升。报道同时指出，英伟达行为准则将个人关系列为可能引发利益冲突的情形，而黄仁勋与Powell均已有配偶。英伟达未回应Tom's Hardware的置评请求。2018年，英特尔前CEO Brian Krzanich也曾因与员工的关系违反公司政策而辞职，成为此类公司治理问题的先例。

这一报道的背景是，英伟达本周早些时候已曝出黄仁勋与Alice Huang的婚外情。Alice Huang曾是新加坡公司Megaspeed的高管，美国情报界认为她疑似为中国从事间谍活动；黄仁勋在致英伟达员工的邮件中承认了这段关系，中国方面否认相关间谍指控。英伟达董事会正在由Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz律所主导调查该事件，黄仁勋在调查期间继续执掌公司。与此同时，多家律所正代表股东起诉英伟达，其中包括一项拟议的集体诉讼，指控公司就业务重大事实误导投资者。美国国会众议院中国问题委员会已要求黄仁勋出席闭门会议，共和党议员称相关报道“引发重大国家安全担忧”。美国总统特朗普则表示FBI正在调查黄仁勋，但又称黄仁勋“完全不知道涉事人员是间谍”。

从行业影响看，黄仁勋是AI芯片行业的核心领导者，英伟达提供当前AI领域最抢手的芯片，他本人也与特朗普政府保持密切接触，并试图影响出口管制政策。因此，这一系列丑闻的直接风险集中在公司治理、合规与利益冲突管理、领导层稳定性、股东诉讼、国家安全审查以及政策游说能力上；对AI芯片产业的技术影响则是间接的——可能影响投资者信心、监管环境和出口政策预期，而非产品技术路线。原文未披露任何芯片架构、核心技术原理、性能参数或产品对比数据，故无法就技术性能层面展开比较。整体而言，事件已从高管个人关系问题扩展为涉及董事会调查、股东诉讼、国会审查和国家安全关切的综合性公司治理危机，英伟达的回应及调查进展将直接影响市场对其管理层稳定性和政策风险的评估。

items.title: OpenAI and Georgia county leaders hit with Mafia-style RICO racketeering lawsuit over $30 billion AI data center
items.description: The plaintiffs alleged that the parties committed fraud and concealment through NDAs and misleading public statements.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Residents of Effingham County, Georgia, just filed a RICO lawsuit against their county commissioners, county leaders, and OpenAI and its affiliates, alleging that they committed various offenses in a conspiracy to get OpenAI’s “Project Camellia” approved. According to the Effingham Herald, the plaintiffs — Dr. Michelle Finch-Mincey, Lehman Mincey Jr., and Raymond Carver — are seeking civil damages, saying that the project has harmed their property values and even pointing out that purchase offers for nearby residential properties have dropped or been withdrawn since the data center was announced.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe lawsuit names all Effingham County Commissioners — Chairperson Damon Rahn, Forrest Floyd, Roger Burdette, Jamie DeLoach, Elizabeth Helmly, and Phil Kieffer — as defendants, alongside County Manager Tim Callanan, Effingham County Industrial Development Authority (IDA) CEO Brandt Herndon, the IDA itself, OpenAI, Octans GA LLC, the entity operating the data center on behalf of OpenAI, and Savannah Industrial Development LLC, the agency involved in the sale of IDA property to Octans and OpenAI.It’s alleged that the defendants committed fraud and concealment through non-disclosure agreements and misleading public statements so that residents remain unaware of the nature of the projects for as long as possible, and that there was a civil conspiracy “to advance Project Camellia through confidential negotiations and closed-door decisions.” They also claimed that the parties engaged in improper land transactions, zoning violations, and civil racketeering.wLatest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Project Camellia is one of OpenAI’s biggest data center projects planned for construction in Effingham County. The site is expected to cost somewhere between $20 billion and $30 billion, to be built across five phases, with a planned compute capacity of 3.2 gigawatts. The company also promised that it will not affect the community’s utility costs, as it will pay for the full cost of all its required infrastructure upgrades, and that it will have minimal water use due to its closed-loop water system. Despite those promises, it seems that some people are opposing the project because of how the county had allegedly tried to secure the land, tax incentives, and zoning approvals without informing the residents until key decisions were finalized and contracts had been signed.The RICO Act — or Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act — was originally conceived as a way to counter organized crime, particularly Mafia leadership, who often used low-level members to commit individual crimes and do the dirty work for them. However, Georgia’s RICO Act is less stringent than the federal version, which is why it’s been used multiple times for cases that seemingly had nothing to do with the Mafia. For example, it was in the 2023 election racketeering case against Donald Trump and 18 others in the attempt to overturn the 2020 U.S. presidential election results in the state, and it was also used in Young Thug’s trial after the rapper was accused of running YSL Records as a criminal street gang. You may like Local opposition blocked $68 billion worth of data center projects in the second quarter of 2026 OpenAI considers rebranding data centers to 'AI compute campuses" as data center backlash intensifies Microsoft-backed AI data center faces backlash over alleged unpermitted gas turbines and 1.5M-gallon LNG tank Critics say that Georgia’s version is way too encompassing, though, and that it was being used to squeeze defendants involved in more mundane or common felonies. “When you have a hammer, everything looks like a nail,” Georgia State University professor of criminal justice and criminology Volkan Topalli said in Atlanta Magazine.The actions of both state officials, OpenAI, and its affiliates are not new, though. There have already been multiple complaints of data center developers and local governments using non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) while they negotiate terms for possible data center projects. Developers say they use this tool to avoid “running afoul of insider trading rules,” but people have pointed out that West Feliciana Parish in Louisiana was able to close a data center deal without resorting to one. An AWS data center in Gilroy, California, is also facing scrutiny after residents only discovered the nature of the project when construction began after a five-year permitting saga that relied on zoning rules that were set 45 years ago.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: OpenAI和佐治亚州县领导因300亿美元AI数据中心遭遇黑手党式RICO敲诈勒索诉讼
items.descriptionZh:
据《Effingham Herald》和Tom's Hardware报道，美国佐治亚州埃芬汉县居民Michelle Finch-Mincey博士、Lehman Mincey Jr.和Raymond Carver已依据佐治亚州《反诈骗及腐败组织法》（RICO）提起诉讼，控告县委员、县领导层以及OpenAI及其关联方在推动OpenAI“Project Camellia”数据中心项目获批过程中涉嫌合谋违法。被告包括全部县委员——主席Damon Rahn，以及Forrest Floyd、Roger Burdette、Jamie DeLoach、Elizabeth Helmly、Phil Kieffer——县经理Tim Callanan、埃芬汉县工业发展局（IDA）及其CEO Brandt Herndon、OpenAI、代表OpenAI运营该数据中心的Octans GA LLC，以及参与IDA向Octans和OpenAI出售土地的Savannah Industrial Development LLC。原告寻求民事赔偿，称项目已损害其房产价值，并指出自数据中心宣布以来，附近住宅的收购报价已经下降或被撤回。

原告的核心指控是：被告通过保密协议（NDA）和误导性公开声明实施欺诈与隐瞒，使居民尽可能长时间不了解项目性质；各方还通过保密谈判和闭门决策推动Project Camellia，涉嫌不当土地交易、违反区划规定和民事敲诈勒索。争议焦点在于，县政府被指在土地、税收优惠和区划审批等关键决策完成、合同签署之前，没有充分告知居民。Project Camellia是OpenAI计划在埃芬汉县建设的最大数据中心项目之一，预计投资200亿至300亿美元，分五期建设，规划算力/电力容量达3.2吉瓦。OpenAI承诺承担全部必要基础设施升级费用，不影响社区公用事业成本，并通过闭环水系统尽量减少用水。技术层面，这不是芯片产品，而是超大规模AI算力基础设施：以吉瓦级电力容量支撑大模型训练和推理，五期滚动建设降低一次性部署风险，闭环水冷则针对数据中心散热和水资源约束；但其治理透明度争议已盖过技术承诺。

RICO原为打击有组织犯罪、尤其是黑手党领导层而设，但佐治亚州版本比联邦版本更宽泛，曾被用于2023年针对特朗普等人的选举敲诈案，以及说唱歌手Young Thug案。批评者认为佐治亚州RICO适用范围过广。此案也折射出AI数据中心选址中的普遍矛盾：开发商和地方政府常用NDA推进谈判，开发商称这是为避免触犯内幕交易规则，但路易斯安那州West Feliciana Parish曾在没有NDA的情况下完成数据中心交易；加州Gilroy的AWS数据中心也因居民直到施工开始才发现项目而受到审视，该案经历了五年许可程序，并依赖45年前制定的区划规则。该诉讼可能影响OpenAI项目推进、当地房产价值和社区关系，并成为AI数据中心选址透明度、公众参与和地方审批程序的重要案例。

items.title: SpaceX develops its own ‘Kessel’ rack-scale system featuring 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for data centers in space, report claims
items.description: SpaceX is reportedly developing a 'Kessel' rack-scale system design with 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs that relies on a massive 84-layer PCB midplane.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter SpaceX/xAI is developing a custom version of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale AI system that replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board (PCB), in part for use in orbital data centers, reports SemiAnalysis. The system is codenamed Kessel and retains 36 Vera CPUs, 72 Rubin GPUs, and nine NVLink switch trays, but introduces a different solid-state interconnect architecture. While SpaceX/xAI will continue to buy Nvidia hardware directly from the company, Elon Musk's company will source other components independently, which could give it greater control over its hardware supply chain.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCThe Kessel system retains the fundamental configuration of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, which comprises 72 GPU packages distributed across 18 compute trays and nine NVLink switch trays. However, instead of Nvidia's conventional arrangement with internal NVLink cable cartridges, SpaceX plans to position compute and switch trays back-to-back around a passive PCB midplane. The architecture resembles a smaller version of Nvidia's Kyber design with 576 AI GPUs (albeit in 144 packages), which also relies on a PCB-based interconnect rather than conventional cable assemblies, SemiAnalysis notes. Interestingly, the design is aimed at both terrestrial and orbital deployments, according to the analysts.Arguably the most distinctive feature of Kessel is its 84-layer PCB midplane, which uses ultra-low-loss M10 copper-clad laminates (CCLs). By contrast, Nvidia's Kyber architecture relied on a backplane based on a considerably more complex 156-layer PCB featuring M9 CCLs. The reduction in layer count by nearly half could substantially improve manufacturability and production yields, but the more advanced copper-clad laminate will almost certainly increase material costs. In any case, an 84-layer PCB is a device that is exceptionally hard to build.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The move to a PCB midplane could simplify system assembly by eliminating numerous high-speed cable connections, but it would not necessarily reduce manufacturing costs. An 84-layer PCB that relies on ultra-low-loss M10 laminate is an exceptionally expensive component that requires sophisticated manufacturing processes and precise quality control. To put an 84-layer PCB number into context, modern high-end server motherboards use 15 – 20 layers, whereas server development boards use more than 20 layers to virtually eliminate any electrical issues with the board itself. Furthermore, manufacturing yields of an 84-layer PCB could become a major obstacle, as defects in internal layers may render an entire board unusable. Consequently, the economic viability of Kessel will depend on whether savings from cable elimination and independent component procurement can offset the cost of its complex midplane.Perhaps more importantly, Kessel represents a departure from Nvidia's conventional system-level procurement model. Instead of purchasing Nvidia's assembled L6 compute boards or even L10 trays that Nvidia plans to sell with its Vera Rubin generation, SpaceX reportedly plans to acquire AI accelerators, CPUs, switches, and networking components directly from Nvidia and procure other components from third-party suppliers (one can wonder how easy it will be for SpaceX/xAI to procure memory amid today's shortages). This would enable SpaceX to select its own PCB manufacturers, component vendors, and manufacturing partners, optimize its hardware for its infrastructure (which will be important for orbital deployments), and perhaps reduce intermediary costs. Meanwhile, the company would assume greater responsibility for system design, validation, manufacturing quality, and supply-chain management, which is something that most hyperscalers have been doing in recent years. You may like SpaceX reportedly seeking $40 billion debt package for Nvidia AI hardware SpaceXAI will deploy standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs for Grok's agentic workloads Chinese AI lab Moonshot reportedly looked at European data centers to access Nvidia chips, report claims For Nvidia, the implications are less straightforward. Although direct sales of CPU and AI GPU packages could reduce the company's revenue from complete compute-board assemblies, the arrangement could also encourage other large customers to develop their own Nvidia-based systems and eventually deploy more Nvidia-based machines, something that may be important in a world where custom silicon developed by hyperscalers is rapidly gaining traction. However, to make this happen, Kessel must be a smashing success that will offer clear advantages over systems designed by Nvidia. items.titleZh: 报道称，SpaceX 开发出自有的“Kessel”机架级系统，搭载 72
items.descriptionZh:
据 SemiAnalysis 报道，SpaceX/xAI 正在开发英伟达 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架级 AI 系统的定制版本，代号 Kessel。该系统最大的变化是用一块大型 84 层印制电路板（PCB）中板替代传统的 NVLink 线缆组件，并计划同时面向地面和轨道数据中心部署。Kessel 仍保留 Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 的基本配置：36 颗 Vera CPU、72 颗 Rubin GPU，以及 9 个 NVLink 交换机托盘；72 个 GPU 封装分布在 18 个计算托盘和 9 个交换机托盘上。不同之处在于，SpaceX 计划把计算托盘和交换机托盘背靠背布置在一块无源 PCB 中板周围，而不是采用 Nvidia 常规的内部 NVLink 线缆盒。这一架构类似 Nvidia Kyber 设计的缩小版：Kyber 面向 576 个 AI GPU（144 个封装），同样依赖 PCB 互连而非传统线缆组件。

Kessel 最引人注目的特点是其 84 层 PCB 中板，采用超低损耗 M10 覆铜板（CCL）。作为对比，Nvidia Kyber 使用的是更复杂的 156 层 PCB 背板，搭配 M9 CCL。将层数减少近一半，可能显著改善可制造性和生产良率，但更先进的覆铜板几乎必然会提高材料成本。84 层 PCB 本身也是极难制造的器件。转向 PCB 中板可以简化系统组装，消除大量高速线缆连接，但并不必然降低制造成本：超低损耗 M10 层压板非常昂贵，需要复杂制造工艺和精确质量控制。作为参照，现代高端服务器主板通常使用 15—20 层，服务器开发板使用 20 层以上以尽量避免板级电气问题。84 层 PCB 的良率可能成为主要障碍，因为内部层缺陷可能导致整块板报废。因此，Kessel 的经济可行性取决于取消线缆和独立采购组件带来的节省，能否抵消复杂中板的成本。

更重要的是，Kessel 偏离了 Nvidia 传统的系统级采购模式。SpaceX 据称不购买 Nvidia 组装的 L6 计算板，也不购买 Nvidia 计划随 Vera Rubin 一代销售的 L10 托盘，而是直接从 Nvidia 采购 AI 加速器、CPU、交换机和网络组件，并从第三方供应商采购其他组件。在当前内存供应紧张的背景下，SpaceX/xAI 如何采购内存也值得关注。这种模式使 SpaceX 可以选择自己的 PCB 制造商、组件供应商和制造伙伴，针对自身基础设施优化硬件，这对轨道部署尤为重要，并可能降低中间成本。但与此同时，SpaceX 将承担更多系统设计、验证、制造质量和供应链管理责任，这也是近年来多数超大规模云厂商正在做的事情。

对 Nvidia 而言，影响并不简单。直接销售 CPU 和 AI GPU 封装可能减少其来自完整计算板组件的收入，但这种安排也可能鼓励其他大客户开发基于 Nvidia 的自有系统，最终部署更多 Nvidia 机器。在超大规模厂商自研芯片迅速崛起的背景下，这一点可能很重要。不过，Kessel 必须取得显著成功，并相比 Nvidia 设计的系统展现出明确优势，这一模式才可能真正推广。

items.title: Softbank loses $3.7 billion on canceled AI data center gas turbine orders days after denying Elon Musk’s claim it was defaulting
items.description: SoftBank might not have defaulted on a raft of gas turbine orders, but it has pulled out of deals for unwanted power units after overestimating how many it could use amid the AI data center buildout boom.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter By early 2026, Japanese tech investment outfit SoftBank had reserved more power generation capacity than the entire state of Connecticut after cornering a huge portion of the global gas turbine production capacity. Now, the same company has chosen to take a $3.7 billion hit to its earnings after canceling reservations for the highly sought-after power generation hardware. The WSJ reports that SoftBank had reserved more than 13 gigawatts of power-producing turbines, citing unnamed "people familiar with the orders." That's the equivalent of more than six Hoover Dams' worth of capacity, with SoftBank founder and chief executive Masayoshi Son believing that it would be vital to the company's earning potential moving forward. Notably, this development surfaced after SoftBank's CFO fired back at Elon Musk's recent revelation that the company had defaulted on turbine blade contracts, saying, "there is no such default."Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe gas turbines were to power AI data centers, and SoftBank is set to build a 9.2-gigawatt power plant in Ohio, with construction scheduled for early 2027. It'll cost $33 billion to build and will provide power to a neighboring eight-gigawatt data center. That data center will be leased to OpenAI, albeit only after Nvidia entered discussions about guaranteeing around $250 billion of financing for the project.But SoftBank got ahead of itself. After initially planning to use the turbines for future gas-powered plants, the company has now chosen to change direction. Orders for turbines, engines that convert natural gas into the electricity used by data centers, must be placed years in advance of them being required. The company had bet big, placing huge orders with the expectation that demand would greatly outstrip supply. That would leave SoftBank in an enviable position, holding huge orders for the vital components required as part of a data center rollout boosted by AI demand. But those reservations weren't cheap — turbine manufacturers regularly charge customers tens of millions of dollars per gigawatt.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: It's now canceled its remaining reservations with GE Vernova, its turbine supplier, while also unwinding contracts for orders that were too far gone. SoftBank told investors on a recent earnings call that the orders had been placed “to secure power generation equipment in anticipation of shortages,” but it now appears it anticipated a little too much.Crucially, SoftBank is also keen for everyone to know that this move was voluntary and that it did not default on its orders. That's contrary to what xAI CEO Elon Musk claimed in a post on his X social network. items.titleZh: 软银因AI数据中心燃气轮机订单被取消损失37亿美元，就在其否认埃隆·马斯克称其违约的几天后
items.descriptionZh:
日本科技投资集团软银在AI数据中心电力需求激增的背景下，曾大举锁定燃气轮机产能：到2026年初，其预留的发电容量甚至超过美国康涅狄格州全州发电能力，并拿下全球燃气轮机产能的很大一部分。据《华尔街日报》报道，软银预留了超过13GW的燃气发电轮机，相当于六个以上胡佛水坝的装机容量。软银创始人兼CEO孙正义认为，这些稀缺设备对公司的未来盈利潜力至关重要。燃气轮机将天然气转化为电能，是数据中心自备电站或并网电站的核心设备；由于制造周期长，相关订单通常需要提前数年下达。软银原本押注AI带来的电力需求将远超供给，因此提前锁定关键设备，希望在未来数据中心建设中占据有利位置。但这类预留并不便宜，轮机制造商通常按每GW数千万美元向客户收费。

如今，软银选择取消剩余预留，并对业绩计入37亿美元冲击。公司取消了向燃气轮机制造商GE Vernova的剩余订单，同时解除了一些“已经推进过远”的合同。软银在近期财报电话会上告诉投资者，这些订单是为了“预判短缺而确保发电设备”，但现在看显然预期过高。相关项目包括在俄亥俄州建设一座9.2GW燃气电站，计划2027年初开工，造价330亿美元，并为邻近一座8GW数据中心供电。该数据中心拟租给OpenAI，但前提包括英伟达就约2500亿美元融资担保进行讨论。软银还特别强调，此次取消是自愿行为，并非违约；公司CFO后藤芳光否认了马斯克在X上所称软银违约涡轮叶片合同的说法，称“这完全不对，不存在这样的违约”。

从技术影响看，AI基础设施的瓶颈正从芯片扩展到电力。燃气发电能够提供稳定基荷电力，并相对可控地快速部署，适合支撑大规模AI数据中心，但需要提前锁定产能、承担巨额资本开支，并面对排放和监管约束。软银的撤退表明，即便AI电力需求长期看涨，提前数年超额预订关键设备也会带来财务和履约风险；同时，电力供应、融资担保和大客户租约正成为AI数据中心能否落地的核心变量。

items.title: ASRock quietly rolls out new firmware after disastrous previous update killed Radeon RX 7900-series GPUs
items.description: Asrock's VBIOS 1.0.6 update follows reports of Radeon RX 7900 XT and XTX graphics cards failing to boot after installing the previous firmware.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter ASRock has rolled out a new firmware update for its Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards. The latest VBIOS version 1.0.6 appears to be a follow-up to the previous 1.0.5 release. According to community reports, that older version was bricking some of the company's Radeon RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX graphics cards. The new update has now quietly made its way to the ASRock official website, although the company has not published a changelog or provided any details on what the new update addresses.Last month, AMD released a VBIOS patch for Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards to address potential security vulnerabilities. While the company did not disclose any technical details about the vulnerabilities, it assured gamers that there had been no reports of them being exploited. According to reports shared with VideoCardz, a user in Japan received a confirmation from ASRock that the failed update would be covered under warranty. However, another owner in Europe was reportedly directed to seek warranty service despite having an out-of-warranty graphics card. This essentially leaves affected owners uncertain of whether they will receive free repairs or replacements. items.titleZh: 华擎在此前灾难性更新导致 Radeon RX 7900 系列 GPU 损坏后悄然推出新固件
items.descriptionZh:
华擎（ASRock）已为其 Radeon RX 7000 系列显卡发布新版 VBIOS 固件 1.0.6，被视为此前 1.0.5 版本的后续更新。事件背景是：社区报告称，华擎此前发布的 1.0.5 VBIOS 导致部分 Radeon RX 7900 XT 和 RX 7900 XTX 显卡无法启动，也就是俗称的“变砖”。新版 1.0.6 已悄然上线华擎官网，但华擎没有发布更新日志，也未说明该版本具体修复了什么问题。

这一轮固件更新的上游背景是 AMD 上月为 Radeon RX 7000 系列发布 VBIOS 补丁，以修复潜在安全漏洞。AMD 未披露漏洞技术细节，但表示没有收到这些漏洞在实际环境中被利用的报告。AMD 在给 ComputerBase 的声明中称，这是其处理潜在安全漏洞的常规做法，相关修正会在公开宣布前提供给客户，以便用户有时间更新固件，并建议用户尽快安装显卡厂商提供的固件更新。

从技术层面看，VBIOS 是显卡的基础固件，负责硬件初始化、供电与频率等底层参数配置，因此固件刷写异常可能导致显卡无法正常点亮。华擎随后曾为 10 款显卡型号列出 1.0.5 VBIOS 更新，覆盖 Radeon RX 7600 XT、RX 7700 XT、RX 7800 XT、RX 7900 XT 和 RX 7900 XTX 系列。但多名 RX 7900 XT 和 RX 7900 XTX 用户报告，安装该固件后系统无法启动；部分用户借助外部 EEPROM 编程器才恢复显卡。华擎已从官网撤下 1.0.5 更新，但尚未说明失败原因，也未确认新发布的 1.0.6 是否解决该问题。

在售后层面，受影响用户的处理方式仍不明确。据报道，一名日本用户获得华擎确认，失败更新将纳入保修范围；但另一名欧洲用户据称被要求走保修服务，而其显卡已过保。这意味着受影响用户仍不确定能否获得免费维修或更换。由于 1.0.6 没有更新日志和官方说明，用户也难以判断安装该替代固件是否安全。原文未提供性能参数或性能对比数据，事件核心并非性能提升，而是安全漏洞修复、固件更新风险及厂商沟通与售后问题。对于游戏玩家和 RX 7000 系列用户而言，是否以及何时安装 1.0.6，目前仍需等待华擎给出更清晰的说明。

items.title: Cognichip reveals how its new AI-assisted program can slash chip design times from months to days — automating labor-intensive tasks cuts design time down, Chief Product Officer explains
items.description: Cognichip claims its AI can slash chip design time from months to days, only that that design must be very simplistic.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Amid the AI gold rush, one particularly fruitful vein of research is the emergence of AI-assisted workflows in electronic design automation (EDA) tools like Cadence Maestro. One such company developing such foundational models is Cognichip, which in September launched Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI), proprietary AI models developed specifically for semiconductor engineering. ACI deploys the 'industry’s largest training dataset' across semiconductor physics and chip design principles.ACI Enterprise is Cognichip's deployable platform, which combines these specialized models with agentic workflows, project memory, and computing infrastructure for AI inference. The company describes ACI's approach as a self-learning flywheel, a continuously evolving design environment that brings together specifications, register-transfer level (RTL), and verification results to build a design that meets power, performance, and area (PPA) targets to Pareto limits. We sat down with Cognichip to learn more."We have surpassed, I think, over ten million training samples in our datasets that are either things that we designed ourselves directly or things that have been generated through our synthetic technology," says Stelios Diamantidis, Chief Product Officer at Cognichip, in an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium. "We have invented new ways of creating synthetic training samples for semiconductor design. And very importantly, now that we have all these data samples, characterized data samples, we also had to invent new models so that we can capture the data, and we also had to invent new pipelines for training so that we can map the training data to the models themselves."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Cognichip)A self-learning flywheelCognichip says ACI can analyze specifications, explore microarchitectural options, generate RTL, verify designs, identify and fix functional problems, and optimize designs to meet PPA targets. The system can also integrate existing IP modules and even produce FPGA implementations. In principle, ACI enables engineers to focus on product requirements and architectural decisions while ACI handles much of the logic implementation and verification work."Build the spec, build the RTL, estimate PPA, perform optimizations, run verification, everything," Diamantidis told us while explaining how ACI can develop and evaluate multiple architectural alternatives before engineers select the preferred design. "We do not try to turn the designer into a verification engine; our system is self-verified, so we want the designer to design, and we want our system not only to do the tasks but also verify them." You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond Because ACI operates as a self-learning flywheel, Cognichip claims engineers can revisit earlier architectural decisions and modify their designs without restarting the entire development process from scratch."Architecture, microarchitecture, RTL, all abstractions in the cognitive system are aligned, so the change in microarchitecture is essentially automatically reflected in RTL, and vice versa," Diamantidis explained. "Changes in RTL are automatically reflected in microarchitecture."Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsCognichip says it has participated in more than 40 customer engagements, including projects at Renesas and SiTime. According to the company, these engagements span a wide range of chip designs, from microcontrollers and encryption engines to networking processors, RISC-V CPUs, and AI accelerators.To illustrate ACI's capabilities, Cognichip points to an evaluation conducted with an unnamed leading fabless semiconductor company. The customer provided an existing 55-page microarchitecture specification, which ACI used to explore architecture options, develop RTL from scratch, and integrate middleware and other components. The system also generated SystemVerilog testbenches, ran simulations, identified and corrected errors, and achieved functional verification closure with over 90% UVM coverage, the company claims. According to Cognichip, the entire process took just 10 days and required only one engineer. By contrast, doing the same job using conventional methods would require a full front-end design team and approximately 20 weeks, Cognichip says.However, there are several important caveats. First up, the customer had already provided a detailed 55-page microarchitecture specification, so the platform did not begin with a blank sheet. Secondly, Cognichip has not disclosed the complexity of the design, which makes it difficult to assess how much work has been done (or rather, processed). Finally, the reported acceleration applies to front-end engineering rather than the entire chip development process, which also includes physical implementation, tape-out, manufacturing, and silicon validation.Making very educated guesses/predictionsThere is a substantial difference between developing functionally, conducting verified RTL, and prepping a chip design for manufacturing. Although Cognichip's ACI can develop microarchitectures, generate RTL, and optimize designs for PPA, the platform does not perform physical implementation. Tasks such as floorplanning, placement and routing, clock-tree synthesis, physical verification, and signoff still require conventional electronic design automation (EDA) tools from companies like Cadence, Synopsys, and Siemens EDA. What to read next OpenAI Jalapeño design interview transcript OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design Cadence reveals Maestro, fine-tuned AI models built to run specialized chip design agents, with early access coming for 'select customers' in Q4 2026 "Today we do not do physical implementation," Diamantidis said. "So, place and route […] is done outside of our system." (Image credit: Cognichip)This distinction matters because an architecture that meets its estimated PPA targets may fail to achieve them after physical implementation. For example, a design expected to operate at 1 GHz while consuming 15 W could achieve only 800 MHz at 20 W once engineers account for interconnect delays, clock distribution, buffering requirements, congestion, and other physical effects. Such discrepancies can require changes to RTL or even fundamental architectural elements, followed by another round of verification and physical implementation. In some cases, these iterations can consume weeks or months of engineering time."That cycle is very expensive in terms of time," Diamantidis said. "Because you are crossing design boundaries, and you are running very long runtimes and all that."Cognichip claims that ACI can reduce these costly iterations by predicting the physical consequences of architectural decisions before implementation begins. According to Diamantidis, the company has trained its models on internally developed and characterized semiconductor designs, which enables ACI to estimate PPA characteristics and identify potential architectural trade-offs during front-end development."We have trained models with full physical stack visibility understanding so that the models can predict the PPA during the front-end design phase." "We can identify those trade-offs before going to physical implementation."For example, ACI could recommend replacing two independent FIFOs with a single time-multiplexed FIFO to reduce power consumption at the expense of performance. Diamantidis used this hypothetical scenario to illustrate how the platform can evaluate architectural alternatives before engineers commit to a particular implementation."If you want to save power here at the cost of 10% of frequency, take these two FIFOs that you have for two different tasks, merge them, make one FIFO, and then time multiplex the two functions over one FIFO," Diamantidis explained.Cognichip claims that ACI can estimate not only the immediate PPA consequences of such changes but also their potential impact on physical implementation."These trade-offs become visible now because we can tell the designer essentially in real time what some of these impacts are going to be to downstream parasitics and downstream congestion and all those kinds of effects."The general idea behind ACI is to resolve potential architectural problems before RTL reaches physical design engineers rather than wait for implementation results and revise the architecture afterward."Our expectation is that there will be no loopbacks to the designer in terms of 'let us do this again because we did not meet this goal or because we ran into congestion issues,'" said Diamantidis.However, the accuracy of these predictions is critical. Cognichip claims its models can predict certain PPA characteristics with errors of approximately 10% relative to results obtained from conventional EDA tools at the pre-route stage of physical implementation.Cognichip evaluated its technology using 1,200 open-source designs and compared its predictions with those produced by general-purpose AI models, including Anthropic's Claude Opus and Google's Gemini. According to him, general-purpose models produced errors of approximately 50% – 100%, depending on the metric, whereas Cognichip's models reduced prediction errors to around 10%."[General purpose models] do not do well when it comes to predicting delays," Diamantidis said. "So, we take that down to within 10%. Again, 10% because think about it, we are running it at RTL. We do not have much physical information at all, right?"There is an important distinction, though. Cognichip's reported accuracy refers to pre-route physical implementation results, not final post-route characteristics. Actual routing introduces interconnect and power delivery parasitics as well as other physical effects that can alter timing and power consumption. Consequently, the reported 10% prediction error does not necessarily mean that ACI-generated designs will achieve their estimated PPA targets after physical implementation and signoff.Another question concerns the range of architectures and manufacturing technologies for which ACI can deliver such accuracy. Although Cognichip says its models incorporate semiconductor physics and account for process-dependent characteristics, it has not disclosed which foundry nodes it supports or how prediction accuracy varies across them.Diamantidis explained that some architectural decisions are largely independent of manufacturing technology, whereas others become increasingly dependent on the target process node as development progresses."[Think about chip development as a tree], at the top of the tree, there are decisions that are not really foundry-specific; they are closer to microarchitecture," he explained. "Then, of course, as you start working your way down the tree, at some point you branch off because the decision may be targeted towards the TSMC node A versus TSMC node B, which will result in different prediction things. But there is a big trunk of decisions that are not really related to the node and are more related to the architecture and the way that the architecture is implemented. What we try to do is we try to think of this whole tree and provide a lot of feedback to designers, especially in a node-agnostic mode, and then, of course, at some point we have to become more node-aware."This distinction is exceedingly important for complex CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators, where physical constraints tend to have substantial impact on architectural decisions. Meanwhile, Cognichip does not claim that ACI must develop such processors as monolithic designs. Instead, the company says its technology can work with individual IP blocks and subsystems, which engineers can subsequently integrate into larger chips. Of course, integration of these individually optimized IP blocks into larger chips is a challenge.Big chip? Not a problem, but there is a caveatAlthough Cognichip says ACI can handle subsystems containing millions of logic gates (i.e., circuits that implement Boolean functions), combining multiple such designs into a complex SoC introduces additional constraints related to interconnect delays, clock distribution, shared memory bandwidth, power delivery, and floorplanning. Consequently, an architecture that achieves Pareto-optimal PPA characteristics as a standalone subsystem may no longer be optimal once integrated into a larger chip. According to Cognichip, ACI can account for these system-level interactions by aligning and optimizing individual blocks against global SoC and subsystem constraints.“Yes, ACI can align and optimize individual blocks to global SoC and subsystem constraints. It can be applied to both flat and hierarchical optimization problems,” Diamanditis said. (Image credit: Cognichip)Cognichip is not proposing a fundamentally new SoC development methodology, but rather automating substantial portions of conventional front-end workflows. Its ACI platform supports both flat and hierarchical optimization and can drive the partitioning and propagation of design constraints from the top level to individual blocks. According to Cognichip, ACI can decompose system-level constraints into requirements for individual components and then re-aggregate them as the blocks are integrated.“ACI does not require a flat design methodology; it can drive hierarchical design from the top or subsystem-top down, ensuring that constraints are decomposed going into components but then re-aggregated when blocks are integrated,” Diamanditis explained.According to Cognichip, ACI can handle individual IP blocks and subsystems containing millions of logic gates, which can subsequently be combined hierarchically into larger SoCs. The company emphasizes that the complexity of individual partitions, rather than their size, determines how effectively ACI can handle them. However, it remains to be seen how effectively ACI can coordinate architectural decisions and optimize PPA across an entire complex SoC in practice. After all, a Pareto-optimal CPU core, memory controller, and interconnect do not necessarily form a Pareto-optimal SoC, as their interactions introduce additional timing, bandwidth, power, and physical constraints.Then again, developers of complex SoCs already address these challenges with hierarchical design methodologies, system-level optimization, and integration, so ACI’s focus on individual subsystems does not necessarily represent a significant limitation.Feedback loops? No need for them!One of the questions that normally occurs when we talk about a tool that is only aimed at the front end of chip development is how it can handle feedback loops from physical implementation (more on this later). Such feedback loops occur when placement and routing reveal problems with timing, power consumption, die area, or routing congestion that cannot be resolved through physical design optimizations alone. In more serious cases, engineers must revise RTL, pipelines, memory hierarchies, or other architectural elements, which requires another round of functional verification, synthesis, and physical implementation. These iterations can take plenty of time and involve multiple engineering teams, which makes them particularly expensive. (Image credit: Cognichip)Cognichip says ACI can use physical implementation results to revise RTL and microarchitecture if necessary, although this is not the company's primary focus. Instead, it aims to prevent costly iterations between front-end and back-end design teams by predicting potential problems before physical implementation begins."We are still focused very much on what we can do in the front end to prevent these situations rather than fix them."If physical implementation reveals problems that require changes to RTL or microarchitecture, engineers can return to ACI with the relevant feedback (Cognichip does not specify with which file format that feedback must be submitted) and use the platform to revise their designs. Yet, ACI cannot resolve issues that require changes to the physical implementation itself, such as clock-tree synthesis or placement and routing."They can come back to our environments to provide additional guidance, additional prompting, additional information," Diamantidis said. "Then based on that information, we can of course perform an adaptation of the design […] if the issue can be addressed in the design itself, then of course we can do that."Since feedback loops are expensive, yet necessary parts of semiconductor chip development flow, I had to ask that question explicitly, and the answer was that there would be no need for feedback loops with ACI. As the question and response require a lot of minutiae, we've added them in full below.Anton Shilov: Can ACI ingest physical implementation reports from Cadence, Synopsys, or Siemens EDA tools, identify architectural bottlenecks, revise the microarchitecture, and RTL, and repeat the process until the design meets its PPA targets?Stelios Diamantidis: Actually, this is where we depart from conventional approaches. We do not need to wait until physical implementation to identify these issues. We have trained models with full physical-stack visibility, which enables them to predict PPA during the front-end design phase.For example, suppose you have one design that operates at a certain frequency and consumes a certain amount of power, and another that runs perhaps 20% slower but consumes significantly less power. We can identify these trade-offs before physical implementation.Ultimately, the changes you want to make involve RTL and design constraints. Traditionally, engineers develop the RTL and constraints and hand them over to the physical implementation team. That team implements the design and reports the results. If the design fails to meet its targets, the front-end team must make changes, and the process starts again.These iterations are very expensive in terms of time because they cross design boundaries and involve tools with long runtimes.By training our models on the full physical stack, we can now provide immediate feedback to front-end designers. For example, we might tell an engineer: 'If you want to reduce power consumption at the cost of 10% of your frequency, take two FIFOs that serve different functions, combine them into one, and time-multiplex the two functions over that FIFO.'That is just one example of a microarchitectural decision. We can make these trade-offs visible to designers in essentially real time because our models can predict their impact on downstream parasitics, routing congestion, and other physical characteristics.As a result, engineers can make these decisions in a closed loop during front-end development. Once they have resolved the microarchitectural trade-offs and produced well-structured RTL, they can hand the design over to the physical implementation team. Of course, the design still has to go through physical implementation tools.Our expectation is that there will be no need to return the design to the front-end team because it failed to meet its targets or encountered congestion problems. That is the fundamental change we aim to bring to the transition between front-end and back-end chip development.Third Party IP? No problemModern SoCs typically combine proprietary logic with third-party IP, including processor cores, memory controllers, interface IP, and other reusable components. However, developers do not necessarily have access to the RTL of licensed IP blocks, and licensing agreements may restrict how such information can be used. This raises the question of how ACI can integrate third-party IP without access to its internal implementation. (Image credit: Cognichip)According to Cognichip, this is not a problem. ACI does not need to examine proprietary RTL to integrate an existing IP block into a larger design. Such IPs provide relevant interface specifications, including pin connections, signals, and their characteristics. ACI can then proceed with necessary integration logic and connect the IP to other subsystems."Most people want to take […] third-party licensed IP and optimize the integration of the IP," claims Diamantidis. "We ourselves do not ingest the guts of the IPs, nor do we try to train on any kind of data related to the IPs."The CPO of Cognichip stressed that ACI Enterprise protects customers' IP within the company's firewalled data centers and prevents it from entering third-party AI training pipelines. The platform provides customer-controlled access to sensitive information, multi-tenant isolation, and security controls validated through a SOC 2 Type II examination. However, these protections do not supersede the licensing restrictions imposed by third-party IP providers.A new offering Cognichip's ACI technology could substantially improve chip development productivity by automating labor-intensive tasks such as architectural exploration, RTL development, verification, and PPA optimization. (Image credit: Cognichip)The company's benchmark with a major chip designer suggests that the potential gains could be considerable, although the complexity of the project remains undisclosed. Such capabilities could be particularly valuable for startups and newcomers to the semiconductor industry, which tend to lack engineering resources and extensive IP portfolios of established chipmakers. By reducing the time, costs, and expertise required to develop custom silicon, ACI could lower the barriers to entry and enable smaller companies to pursue a custom silicon strategy that would otherwise be prohibitively expensive.However, Cognichip has yet to demonstrate autonomous development of a complete, physically validated chip, let alone a sophisticated CPU or GPU. The company does not perform physical implementation, and its expectations of eliminating costly feedback loops depend on the accuracy of its PPA predictions. It also remains to be seen how effectively ACI can optimize complex SoCs that combine numerous proprietary and third-party IP blocks under common power, performance, and area constraints.Ultimately, the Cognichip technology's value for leading-edge chip developers will depend not only on how quickly it can produce verified RTL, but also on how closely its predictions match the results of physical implementation and how much engineering work it can eliminate across the entire development cycle.

items.titleZh: Cognichip 揭示其新 AI 辅助程序如何将芯片
items.descriptionZh:
在AI热潮推动下，电子设计自动化（EDA）领域正出现越来越多AI辅助工作流，Cadence Maestro等工具是代表之一。Cognichip则进一步尝试用专门面向半导体工程的基础模型改造芯片前端设计流程。该公司于9月推出Artificial Chip Intelligence（ACI），称这是专为半导体工程开发的专有AI模型，并使用其所谓“业界最大训练数据集”覆盖半导体物理和芯片设计原理。其可部署平台ACI Enterprise将专用模型与代理式工作流、项目记忆和用于AI推理的计算基础设施结合起来。公司把ACI的方法描述为“自学习飞轮”：一个持续演进的设计环境，把规格、寄存器传输级（RTL）和验证结果结合起来，以在帕累托极限内满足功耗、性能和面积（PPA）目标。

Cognichip首席产品官Stelios Diamantidis在接受采访时表示，其数据集已超过1000万个训练样本，这些样本要么由公司直接设计，要么通过合成技术生成。公司称还发明了为半导体设计创建合成训练样本的新方法，并开发了新模型和新训练管线，以便捕获数据并将训练数据映射到模型。按照Cognichip的描述，ACI能够分析规格、探索微架构选项、生成RTL、验证设计、识别并修复功能问题，并优化设计以满足PPA目标；系统还可集成现有IP模块，甚至生成FPGA实现。其目标是让工程师聚焦产品需求和架构决策，而把大量逻辑实现和验证工作交给ACI。Diamantidis强调，系统是自验证的，不希望把设计师变成验证引擎，而是让设计师继续做设计，系统不仅完成任务，还验证任务结果。由于ACI以自学习飞轮方式运行，工程师可回到早先架构决策并修改设计，而不必从头重启整个开发流程。公司称架构、微架构和RTL等抽象在认知系统中是对齐的，微架构变化会自动反映到RTL，反之亦然。

Cognichip称已参与40多个客户合作项目，包括Renesas和SiTime的项目，覆盖微控制器、加密引擎、网络处理器、RISC-V CPU和AI加速器等多种芯片设计。为展示能力，公司提到与一家未具名领先无晶圆厂半导体公司的评估：客户提供一份55页的现有微架构规格，ACI据此探索架构选项、从零开发RTL、集成中间件等组件，生成SystemVerilog测试平台、运行仿真、识别并修正错误，并以超过90%的UVM覆盖率实现功能验证收敛。Cognichip称整个过程仅用10天、只需一名工程师；若用传统方法，同样工作需完整前端设计团队和约20周。不过文章也列出重要限定：客户已提供详细微架构规格，平台并非从白纸开始；Cognichip未披露设计复杂度，难以判断实际处理工作量；所称加速仅适用于前端工程，而非包括物理实现、流片、制造和硅验证的完整芯片开发流程。

ACI与完整芯片设计之间的关键差别在于，功能可用、经验证的RTL与可制造芯片设计不是一回事。尽管ACI可开发微架构、生成RTL并优化PPA，但不执行物理实现。布局规划、布局布线、时钟树综合、物理验证和签核仍需要Cadence、Synopsys和Siemens EDA等传统EDA工具。Diamantidis明确表示，目前不做物理实现，布局布线在系统之外完成。这一区分很重要，因为一个在估算中满足PPA目标的架构，在物理实现后可能达不到目标。例如设计预期以1 GHz运行、功耗15 W，但考虑互连延迟、时钟分布、缓冲需求、拥塞等物理效应后，可能只能达到800 MHz、20 W。此类偏差可能要求修改RTL甚至基本架构元素，然后再次验证和物理实现，某些情况下迭代会耗费数周或数月工程时间。Diamantidis称这种循环在时间上非常昂贵，因为跨越设计边界且运行时间很长。

Cognichip声称ACI可通过在物理实现前预测架构决策的物理后果来减少昂贵迭代。公司称其模型在内部开发和表征的半导体设计上训练，具有“完整物理栈可见性”，可在前端设计阶段预测PPA并识别潜在架构权衡。例如ACI可能建议把两个独立FIFO合并为一个时分复用FIFO，以牺牲性能换取功耗降低；Diamantidis用假设场景说明，若想省电而牺牲10%频率，可把两个不同任务的FIFO合并，让两个功能在一个FIFO上时分复用。公司称ACI不仅能估算此类变化的直接PPA后果，还能预测其对下游寄生、拥塞等物理实现影响的潜力，目标是在RTL进入物理设计团队之前解决潜在架构问题，而不是等实现结果出来再修改架构。Diamantidis表示，期望不会因为未达标或拥塞问题而把设计退回前端团队。

但预测准确性至关重要。Cognichip称其模型在物理实现预布线阶段对某些PPA特性的预测误差约为10%，相对传统EDA工具结果而言。公司用1200个开源设计评估技术，并与Anthropic Claude Opus和Google Gemini等通用AI模型比较；据称通用模型按指标不同误差约50%至100%，而Cognichip模型把预测误差降至约10%。Diamantidis称通用模型在预测延迟方面表现不佳。不过，这一准确度指的是预布线物理实现结果，而非最终布线后特性；实际布线会引入互连和供电寄生及其他物理效应，可能改变时序和功耗。因此10%误差不代表ACI生成的设计在物理实现和签核后一定能达到估算PPA目标。另一个问题是ACI在哪些架构和制造工艺上能保持这种准确度。Cognichip称模型纳入半导体物理并考虑工艺相关特性，但未披露支持哪些代工厂节点及不同节点下预测准确度如何变化。Diamantidis解释，芯片开发像一棵树，树冠顶部许多决策并非代工厂特定，更接近微架构；越往下越可能针对台积电节点A或节点B分支，产生不同预测结果；但大量主干决策与节点关系不大，更多与架构及实现方式有关。公司试图覆盖整棵树并向设计师提供大量反馈，尤其以节点无关模式，随后在某个阶段必须更具节点感知能力。这一区分对复杂CPU、GPU和AI加速器尤其重要，因为物理约束往往对架构决策影响很大。Cognichip并不声称ACI必须把这类处理器作为单体设计开发，而是称技术可处理单个IP块和子系统，工程师可随后集成到更大芯片中；当然，把这些分别优化的IP块集成进更大芯片仍是挑战。

Cognichip称ACI可处理包含数百万逻辑门的子系统，但把多个此类设计组合成复杂SoC会引入互连延迟、时钟分布、共享内存带宽、供电和布局规划等额外约束。因此，作为独立子系统实现帕累托最优PPA的架构，集成到更大芯片后可能不再最优。公司称ACI可通过按全局SoC和子系统约束对齐并优化单个模块来考虑这些系统级交互。Diamantidis表示，ACI可把单个模块与全局SoC和子系统约束对齐优化，适用于扁平化和层次化优化问题。Cognichip并非提出全新的SoC开发方法，而是自动化传统前端工作流中的很大一部分。ACI支持扁平化和层次化优化，可驱动设计约束从顶层向单个模块划分和传播；公司称ACI可把系统级约束分解为组件需求，并在模块集成时重新聚合。Diamantidis称ACI不要求扁平设计方法，可从顶层或子系统顶层驱动层次化设计，确保约束分解进入组件，并在模块集成时重新聚合。公司强调，决定ACI处理效果的是单个分区的复杂度而非规模；但ACI在实践中能否有效协调整个复杂SoC的架构决策并优化PPA仍有待观察。毕竟，一个帕累托最优的CPU核心、内存控制器和互连不一定组成帕累托最优SoC，因为它们之间的交互会引入额外时序、带宽、功耗和物理约束。不过，复杂SoC开发者本来就通过层次化设计方法、系统级优化和集成应对这些挑战，因此ACI聚焦单个子系统未必是重大局限。

关于前端工具如何处理物理实现反馈循环，Cognichip称ACI可在必要时利用物理实现结果修改RTL和微架构，但这不是主要焦点。公司更希望在前端预测潜在问题，避免前后端团队之间昂贵迭代。Diamantidis称公司仍非常聚焦前端能做什么来预防这些情况，而不是修复它们。如果物理实现暴露需要修改RTL或微架构的问题，工程师可带着相关反馈回到ACI环境，公司未说明反馈必须以何种文件格式提交，然后基于信息调整设计；但ACI不能解决需要改变物理实现本身的问题，如时钟树综合或布局布线。Diamantidis称客户可回到其环境提供额外指导、提示和信息，基于这些信息可对设计进行适配；如果问题能在设计本身解决，当然可以做。文章作者询问ACI能否摄取Cadence、Synopsys或Siemens EDA工具的物理实现报告，识别架构瓶颈、修改微架构和RTL并重复直到满足PPA目标。Diamantidis回答称这正是其偏离传统方法之处：不需要等到物理实现才识别问题，模型具有完整物理栈可见性，可在前端预测PPA。例如一个设计以某频率运行并消耗一定功耗，另一个可能慢20%但功耗显著更低，可在物理实现前识别这些权衡。最终要做的改变涉及RTL和设计约束。传统上工程师开发RTL和约束交给物理实现团队，团队实现并报告结果；若未达标，前端团队修改，流程重新开始。这些迭代时间成本很高，因为跨设计边界且工具运行时间长。通过在全物理栈上训练模型，可在前端立即反馈，例如告诉工程师若想省电而牺牲10%频率，可把两个不同功能FIFO合并并时分复用。这只是微架构决策的一个例子。公司模型可预测对下游寄生、布线拥塞等物理特性的影响，使工程师在前端开发中以闭环方式做决策。解决微架构权衡并生成结构良好的RTL后，再交给物理实现团队；设计仍须经过物理实现工具。公司期望不会因为未达标或拥塞问题而把设计退回前端，这是其希望在前端和后端芯片开发衔接处带来的根本变化。

对于第三方IP，现代SoC通常把专有逻辑与处理器核心、内存控制器、接口IP等第三方IP结合，但开发者未必能访问授权IP块的RTL，许可协议也可能限制信息使用。Cognichip称这不是问题：ACI不需要检查专有RTL即可把现有IP块集成到更大设计。此类IP提供相关接口规格，包括引脚连接、信号及其特性，ACI可据此推进必要集成逻辑并把IP连接到其他子系统。Diamantidis称多数人想拿第三方授权IP并优化IP集成，但公司本身不摄取IP内部，也不尝试训练任何与IP相关的数据。他强调ACI Enterprise在公司防火墙数据中心内保护客户IP，防止其进入第三方AI训练管线；平台提供客户控制的敏感信息访问、多租户隔离和通过SOC 2 Type II审查验证的安全控制。不过这些保护不能取代第三方IP提供方施加的许可限制。

总体来看，Cognichip的ACI技术有望通过自动化架构探索、RTL开发、验证和PPA优化等劳动密集型任务，显著提高芯片开发生产力。公司与一家大型芯片设计商的基准测试暗示潜在收益可观，但项目复杂度未披露。此类能力对半导体初创公司和行业新进入者尤其有价值，因为他们往往缺乏成熟芯片公司的工程资源和广泛IP组合。通过降低定制硅开发所需时间、成本和专业知识，ACI可能降低进入门槛，使较小公司能够推行原本过于昂贵的定制硅战略。然而，Cognichip尚未展示自主开发完整且经过物理验证的芯片，更不用说复杂CPU或GPU。公司不执行物理实现，其消除昂贵反馈循环的期望取决于PPA预测准确性。ACI能否在共同功耗、性能和面积约束下有效优化结合众多专有和第三方IP块的复杂SoC，也仍有待观察。最终，对领先芯片开发者而言，Cognichip技术的价值不仅取决于多快生成经验证的RTL，还取决于其预测与物理实现结果的匹配程度，以及能在整个开发周期中消除多少工程工作。

items.title: Congress could issue subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he doesn’t respond by today to request for a ‘joint, closed-door briefing’
items.description: Three committee chairpersons want to grill Jensen Huang about his company's 'security protocols against foreign adversary espionage,' as a former CIA agent says that he had a target on his back as the leader of a trillion-dollar company.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 11 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Rep. Brian Mast (R-Fla.), the chairperson of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has said that he will issue a subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he does not respond to the committee’s request to meet with them on November 18 by Wednesday, November 11, according to ABC News. The House invited him to a “joint, closed-door briefing” with the heads of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence, and that they will focus on his company’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.”Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedCongress first called the embattled CEO on November 7, a few days after rumors started circulating about Huang’s “closeness” to a particular Chinese executive suspected of passing information to Chinese intelligence. The following day, Nvidia released a statement from Jensen admitting to an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, apologizing for his unfaithfulness, while the company’s board of directors confirmed it will launch an independent investigation regarding the allegations that the CEO has been specifically targeted by China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS). Aside from having to face Congress, Jensen Huang is also reportedly being looked into by the FBI.It remains unclear whether Jensen Huang was targeted by intelligence agencies, but he came into prominence with the AI boom that was arguably fueled by Nvidia’s AI chips. This led to the AI race as we know it today, with the U.S. taking steps to delay China’s advancement for fears that it will use the technology for military purposes. We also don’t know if Huang Le or Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy or an “innocent” bystander caught in a web of accusations. And, even if she did work with the MSS, the question remains as to whether she specifically targeted the Nvidia CEO or whether Chinese intelligence discovered their indiscretion and used that as a convenient tool for blackmail to extract information from her.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, former CIA agent Darrel Blocker told ABC News that the authorities should just focus on Jensen. “I think that the biggest concern is that the focus or overfocus on just Jensen Huang and Nvidia risks losing sight of the fact that other people have been targeted by the Chinese. Are they talking to the engineers? Are they talking to other people who might have even more access than even the CEO has? So, this focus should not be singular; it should include everyone in the company, and quite frankly, every tech company out there should be looking at all the contacts that their officers and employees have.”“It’s definitely not a one-time thing. When you run a trillion-dollar company, you know that you have a bullseye on your back; whether it’s from competition or rather from nation-states, so this is absolutely not a one-off. Jensen Huang is not the only person at Nvidia that has access to the crown jewels, so I would be looking at the other people in terms of the access that they enjoy and their proximity to Chinese nationals.” You may like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy Nvidia's Jensen Huang officially called to Congress due to reports of a Chinese spy plot US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors

items.titleZh: 若英伟达CEO黄仁勋今日前不回应“联合闭门简报”请求，国会或向其发出传票
items.descriptionZh:
美国众议院外交事务委员会主席、佛罗里达州共和党众议员布莱恩·马斯特表示，如果英伟达CEO黄仁勋不在11月11日（周三）前回应委员会提出的11月18日会面请求，他将向黄仁勋发出传票。据ABC News报道，众议院邀请黄仁勋与负责中国、外交事务和情报事务的多个委员会负责人举行“联合闭门简报”，重点讨论英伟达“防范外国对手间谍活动的安全协议”。

事件背景是，国会最初于11月7日联系黄仁勋，而此前几天出现传闻称，黄仁勋与一名疑似向中国情报机构传递信息的中国高管关系密切。次日，英伟达发布黄仁勋声明，承认与Megaspeed高管Alice Huang存在婚外情，并为不忠道歉；公司董事会确认将就“CEO被中国国家安全部（MSS）针对性针对”的指控启动独立调查。另有报道称，黄仁勋还正被FBI调查。

报道同时强调多项关键事实仍不确定：目前不清楚黄仁勋是否确实被情报机构针对；也不清楚Alice Huang究竟是间谍，还是被卷入指控的“无辜”旁观者；即便她与中国国安部有关，她是否专门针对英伟达CEO，还是中国情报机构发现其不当关系后借机敲诈获取信息，仍无定论。前CIA特工达雷尔·布洛克对ABC News表示，当局不应只盯着黄仁勋，因为“英伟达并非只有CEO能接触核心机密”，其他工程师和员工也可能成为目标；他建议调查应覆盖公司内所有可能接触敏感信息的人，并称所有科技公司都应审查高管和员工与中方人员的接触。

文章还链接了美国对华芯片制裁反复、中国推进自主芯片供应链、华为昇腾NPU路线图、长鑫存储目标2030年占据30% DRAM市场份额以及中国稀土出口管制等背景报道。整体来看，这一事件发生在AI芯片推动全球AI竞赛、美国担忧中国将相关技术用于军事目的并限制对华技术出口的背景下，凸显AI芯片龙头企业在美中科技竞争中所面临的安全、合规与政治风险。原文未涉及具体芯片性能参数或技术对比数据。

items.title: Cyanogen co-founder unveils Kora, a Linux OS that splits AI models across the CPU, GPU, and NPU
items.description: Kora, a Linux desktop OS with built-in AI models and agents for local agentic work, is coming to PCs in 2027, including Snapdragon X2 Elite machines.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A team led by Cyanogen co-founder Kirt McMaster has unveiled Kora, a new Linux desktop OS with integrated AI models and agents that can split workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU resources, as well as other machines on the same local network. We reached out to the firm for more info.Kora, the first product from Kora Systems Inc., previously Playtron, carries the tagline “The Operating System for Intelligence” and has its own Cortex “hybrid inference engine” technology, which is not open source and is optimized for local models. The OS, built “from the kernel to the shell,” runs local models by default and cloud models when needed, and is expected to arrive on PCs in 2027.The desktop follows the AI-focused motif with “neural workspaces” and a “neural file system,” which refer to sandboxed workspaces and files indexed by semantic meaning. Kora has three operating modes: “Work," "Create," and "Play." That last base is covered by GameFrame, which descends from Playtron’s GameOS. Humain OS, which Kora is developing with Saudi AI company Humain, is the enterprise variant of this OS.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Currently, the only NPU named in the release material is the Hexagon NPU found in the Snapdragon X2 Elite, which Qualcomm pegs at 80 TOPS. On the X2 Elite, Cortex can schedule AI workloads across the CPU, GPU, and NPU, as well as other systems on the local network, which could be a novel capability if it works beyond the Qualcomm hardware.McMaster told Tom’s Hardware that the Snapdragon X2 Elite NPU runs Google's Gemma 4 26B model at 25 tokens per second for decode. Intel and AMD NPU support is in the works, but according to the developer, neither NPU will be used for LLMs, as GPUs are “just better for LLM workloads on x64.” You may like Open source project renders your Windows 11 desktop using the NPU rather than the GPU Old MacBook uses a mirror, webcam, and AI agent to code its own AMD GPU drivers Stripped-down Windows 11 for AI developers demands 64GB RAM and insane 250 GB/s bandwidth Each NPU vendor has its own software stack, or runtime, and prefers that models are compiled in its own format: Qualcomm with QAIRT/QNN, Intel with OpenVINO, and AMD with Ryzen AI software. The press kit doesn't identify support for any Intel or AMD chip, NPU runtime, model format, quantization, or speed figures for those platforms.Our earlier Windows testing showed the same kind of divide: Snapdragon reached its NPU through the QNN provider under ONNX Runtime, while Intel’s work ran through IPEX, its extension for PyTorch, on the GPU because it was faster than the NPU.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsWhen asked about cross-vendor support, McMaster reiterated that “only Hexagon on Snapdragon X2 Elite is supported today.” Intel NPU support is planned, with “conversations underway,” though McMaster later clarified that neither Intel’s nor AMD’s NPU will be used for LLMs. On AMD’s Ryzen AI chips, Kora will likely use the NPU for embedding and speech-recognition models through ONNX.As for what drives the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU, McMaster said Kora uses the “llama.cpp Hexagon backend” and “the upstream FastRPC driver.” That suggests the operating system reaches the NPU through the open-source llama.cpp project, not Qualcomm’s own QAIRT/QNN runtime, by way of the FastRPC driver in the mainline kernel. Swipe to scroll horizontally Kora NPU support by vendor, per the company NPU Vendor’s own framework Status in Kora Runtime KORA uses What it runs Qualcomm Hexagon (Snapdragon X2 Elite) QAIRT/QNN Supported today llama.cpp’s Hexagon backend Language models; KORA cites Gemma 4 26B at 25 tokens per second AMD XDNA 2 (Ryzen AI) Ryzen AI software Planned for launch ONNX Likely embedding and speech-recognition models; not language models Intel NPUs OpenVINO Planned, “conversations underway” Not stated Not language models When asked about model formats, McMaster said, “we predominantly support GGUF,” llama.cpp’s model file format, and that Lemma, the inference engine inside Cortex, “can split model layers across processors as needed.” Lemma is built on llama.cpp, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion.cpp, and ONNX. McMaster says that which runtime is used depends on the model's requirements, and more runtimes will be added down the line.For today, llama.cpp has a Hexagon backend for Snapdragon and an OpenVINO backend for Intel CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, although the latter is still marked “In Progress,” and no AMD NPU backend, which would explain why AMD goes through ONNX. AMD NPUs can run LLMs on Linux through the separate Lemonade 10.0 stack with FastFlowLM, as reported by Phoronix in March, though that isn’t the route Kora has chosen. What to read next AI model gets a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled directly into its weights, then runs DOOM on it Geekbench 7 results suggest OpenAI's dots run on nine-core AMD EPYC VMs Minisforum launches local AI solutions at IFA 2026 Beyond NPU stacks, those hoping to run Kora will need to be mindful of their system's available memory. The Gemma 4 26B model Kora uses, which Google lists as Gemma 4 26B A4B, needs about 14.4GB of memory to load its weights at 4-bit (Q4_0) quantization, by Google’s estimate, before any context window, while third-party listings put the download for the Q4_K_M file Kora uses at about 16–17GB. The model only activates about 4 billion of its 26 billion parameters per token but still needs to be fully loaded into memory.McMaster said that with the model, the X2 Elite reaches “25 TPS decode throughput and 550 TPS prefill throughput,” or tokens per second, running “entirely on the Hexagon NPU with 32K context.” A dense model, rather than a mixture-of-experts, would be far slower. Not given are the RAM configuration or the specific X2 Elite chip.On memory, McMaster said that “we recommend 64GB because it gives you access to better models,” but that is not a firm requirement. The company projects that “about 70 percent of the model calls it manages will run locally in 2027.”Kora says its enterprise-focused Humain OS is due first and will be “commercially available in 2027,” on OEM PCs using the Snapdragon X2 Elite. Kora will follow "later in 2027.”McMaster says that “Kora will be posted on our site and downloadable for anyone to install.” Included will be a list of recommended configurations, “but it should be installable on most modern PCs.” Exact pricing and the overall business model will be shared closer to the date of availability.Edit: 11/11/2026 9:06am PT: Added further follow-up details provided by the maker.
