items.titleZh: Cyanogen 联合创始人推出 Kora：一款
items.descriptionZh:
Cyanogen联合创始人Kirt McMaster领导的团队发布了Kora，这是一款面向AI时代的Linux桌面操作系统，由Kora Systems Inc.（前身为Playtron）推出，口号是“The Operating System for Intelligence”。Kora从内核到桌面shell完整构建，默认在本地运行AI模型，在需要时调用云端模型，并集成AI模型与智能体。其核心是自研、非开源的Cortex“混合推理引擎”，针对本地模型优化。Kora计划于2027年登陆PC，企业版本Humain OS则与沙特AI公司Humain合作开发。

Kora围绕AI重构桌面体验，提供“神经工作区”和“神经文件系统”，前者指沙箱化工作区，后者指按语义索引文件。系统有三种模式：工作、创作和游戏；游戏能力由GameFrame支持，技术源自Playtron的GameOS。企业版Humain OS将率先商业化。

技术实现上，Cortex内部的Lemma推理引擎基于llama.cpp、whisper.cpp、stable-diffusion.cpp和ONNX，主要支持GGUF模型格式，并能按需把模型层拆分到不同处理器上运行；具体使用哪种运行时取决于模型需求，未来还会增加更多运行时。Kora可在CPU、GPU、NPU以及同一局域网内的其他机器之间调度AI负载。目前发布材料中明确支持的NPU只有高通骁龙X2 Elite中的Hexagon NPU，Qualcomm给出的算力为80 TOPS。Kora通过llama.cpp的Hexagon后端和上游FastRPC驱动访问该NPU，而不是高通的QAIRT/QNN运行时。Intel NPU支持仍在推进中，官方称“对话正在进行”；AMD Ryzen AI的XDNA 2 NPU计划在发布时支持。但McMaster明确表示，Intel和AMD的NPU都不会用于大语言模型，因为在x64平台上GPU对LLM负载更合适；AMD NPU预计通过ONNX承担嵌入和语音识别等模型。

性能方面，Kora给出的数据显示，在骁龙X2 Elite上，Google Gemma 4 26B模型可完全运行在Hexagon NPU上，32K上下文下实现25 tokens/s的解码吞吐和550 tokens/s的预填充吞吐。该模型为Gemma 4 26B A4B，属于混合专家模型，总参数26B，但每个token仅激活约4B参数，仍需完整加载到内存。按Google估算，4位Q4_0量化下仅权重就需约14.4GB内存，尚未计入上下文窗口；第三方资料显示Kora使用的Q4_K_M文件下载大小约16–17GB。Kora建议64GB内存以便运行更好的模型，但这不是硬性要求。公司预计2027年其管理的模型调用中约70%将在本地运行。

这一方案的意义在于推动“本地优先”的AI PC体验：降低云端依赖、提升隐私和离线可用性，并通过NPU、GPU、CPU及局域网设备协同扩展本地推理能力。不过，它也面临NPU厂商运行时和模型格式碎片化、跨平台支持有限、内存需求高等挑战。发布计划上，面向企业的Humain OS将率先在2027年通过采用骁龙X2 Elite的OEM PC商业化上市，Kora随后于2027年晚些时候推出，并可在官网下载安装，官方将提供推荐配置列表，称其应可安装在大多数现代PC上；具体定价和商业模式将在临近上市时公布。

items.title: AMD shares how it can retain 95% of server performance with just half the DRAM, sidestepping memory shortages with MEXT
items.description: Following AMD’s acquisition of MEXT earlier this year, the company has revealed its own IT infrastructure is using the technology to run servers at 50% DRAM capacity while achieving 95% of the performance of a full-DRAM system in certain applications.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In June, AMD overtook the predictive memory engine known as MEXT, which claims to offer upwards of 99% of the performance of a system with full DRAM capacity while running with as little as 25% of the physical DIMMs. The technology offloads cold memory pages to flash storage and uses an AI model to serve pages before they’re needed, and AMD says it plans to extend the tech across a wide swath of its IT infrastructure next year.The pitch behind MEXT seems too good to be true. According to AMD and MEXT founder Gary Smerdon, the technology can cut the physical DRAM required in a server by 20% to 75% depending on the application and performance target. That missing memory still registers as installed DRAM to the OS. Instead of DRAM, however, MEXT uses relatively inexpensive flash storage to offload cold pages, flying them back in as they’re needed with an AI model. In some of AMD’s internal workloads, such as Synopsys PrimeTime, the company says it’s able to achieve 95% of the performance of a full server while running at 50% DRAM capacity with MEXT.AMD has deployed MEXT internally on 145 servers, which it says will expand to 2,000 servers next year. In addition, the company has announced a partnership with HPE to bring MEXT to customers. Currently, we’re in phase 1 of the rollout, with some EPYC Venice servers carrying a “MEXT Ready” badge and a dedicated NVMe drive or bay for the offload. Phase 2 brings MEXT licenses out to these servers, as well as the RAM View application. AMD hasn’t said when Phase 2 will begin.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The AI-driven DRAM pricing surge impacts more than just gaming PCs, with enterprises also feeling the brunt of price increases, even if they aren’t running AI workloads. If MEXT is able to achieve what AMD claims, it could be transformative given the current market. Because of that, it’s worth understanding what exactly MEXT is, as well as what AMD claims it can do.Although MEXT is exciting in concept, it’s obvious that AMD is taking a conservative approach to the rollout. Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, after all. The applications of MEXT are currently narrow, though AMD says it’s expanding the workloads it’s using MEXT on with promising early results. You may like Marvell VP pushes for DDR4 recycling for use in CXL memory, amid the worst DRAM shortage in years — company introduces three-tier AI memory infrastructure Micron announces 512GB DDR5-9200 memory modules with 16W power draw AMD debuts Helion reference design for agentic AI servers with up to 32,768 Zen 6 ‘Venice’ cores DRAM, Flash and an LLM (Image credit: AMD)The basic setup of MEXT is simple in concept: cold pages go to flash, AI brings those pages back as needed, and it’s as if the memory was never missing in the first place. The main problem should be obvious. Flash is orders of magnitude slower than DRAM, so streaming pages back into memory from flash as they’re needed isn’t feasible. MEXT’s trick is using an AI model to predict the pages you’ll need. And, as long as the model is able to stay ahead by at least the transfer latency from the SSD, it’s as if the physical DRAM was installed the whole time.This isn’t a crazy concept considering how a transformer-based LLM, which MEXT uses, operates. If you’re unfamiliar with the inner workings, this open-source visualization breaks down the concept of a transformer AI model cleanly. The foundational concept is next token prediction, which underpins the design of modern LLMs. Given a set of tokens, the LLM determines which token (word, portion of a word, etc.) is most likely to come next. It makes a prediction. In the case of MEXT, it’s predicting what page is needed next, not what word comes next. (Image credit: AMD)Memory offloading to flash isn’t a new concept, but MEXT founder Gary Smerdon says that AI is the critical difference in this technology. MEXT itself is deployed as a Linux kernel module that works with any Linux distro. It uses an “ensemble of AI models,” with the primary transformer-based LLM driving the technology. And critically, it doesn’t come pre-trained.Instead, AMD says that MEXT trains in under a second when first deployed, operates on one EPYC core without a GPU, and continually trains as the workload progresses. This approach makes sense given the varied workloads that MEXT may apply to. The idea is that it would learn the access patterns of the application in order to drive that prediction engine.MEXT isn’t perfect, but it doesn’t need to be perfect in every situation. For instance, the order of stored pages isn’t important. With text, an LLM needs to predict the correct text in the correct order, but with MEXT, the order doesn’t matter. As long as the page is in DRAM when it’s needed, that’s fine. What to read next AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ deep dive and benchmarking Micron details ambitious DRAM and NAND roadmap — 3D NAND, High-NA EUV, new materials, and custom silicon makes a comeback CXMT president says company’s first 4F² DRAM will be a server DDR5 RDIMM due by year-end In order to understand the application of MEXT to different workloads, AMD has developed RAM View to go alongside the tech. It’s a memory utilization tool that shows which pages are hot and which have gone cold. As you can see from the example above, a system with 1.5 TB of memory shows near-full utilization across the full workload, but around half of the pages stored in memory haven’t been touched in five minutes or more at any given time.AMD provided this generalized example and didn’t clarify what workload it was testing. That’s very important, as the utilization breakdown will look vastly different depending on the application(s) running on the server. Initially, AMD is applying MEXT to critical EDA applications it uses internally, such as Synopsys PrimeTime, but the company says it has focused on optimizing agentic AI, database, and media and entertainment workloads as well. (Image credit: AMD)This is important not only because memory access patterns change between applications, but also because performance in those applications reacts differently when a system doesn’t have enough memory. The “memory wall,” as AMD calls it, should be a familiar concept regardless of whether you’ve ever touched a server. With MEXT, AMD says it’s trying to extend this memory wall, which may look different for different applications.For instance, the company is confident that many workloads can reduce capacity by around 20% to 25%. As the reduction increases, however, the applications become more specialized, and the performance delta becomes greater.AMD’s internal MEXT results (Image credit: AMD)AMD has shared some internal MEXT results, which look impressive, though as usual, it’s always smart to handle first-party benchmarks like this with skepticism. Starting with PrimeTime, where AMD has focused much of its attention on MEXT up to this point, it says servers running at 50% capacity retain 95% of the performance of a full server, and going down to as little as 25% capacity still maintains 80% of the application’s performance. (Image credit: AMD)PrimeTime demands a lot of memory for large designs. There are some applications where performance is nearly identical, according to AMD. In a 3-node cluster running in Azure with 5th-gen EPYC CPUs, AMD says MEXT offers 99% of the performance of the full cluster while running at 50% DRAM capacity with the Spark SQL workload from the TPC-DS benchmark. SQL databases try to cache as much data as possible in memory to prevent I/O bottlenecks, creating a golden opportunity for tech like MEXT that wants to free cold pages. (Image credit: AMD)Perhaps the most applicable workload at the current moment, however, is agentic AI, and AMD says MEXT has similar applications there. Across a five-agent concurrent geomean, AMD claims 99% of the performance of a full server with 50% memory capacity, and 85% of the performance with 25% capacity. With a “memory-hungry” agent, AMD claims 90% and 88% performance for 50% and 25% capacity, respectively.The slide you can see above has footnote tags. However, AMD has not shared the footnotes with us yet, so we don’t have a view into how these tests were run. Naturally, we assume AMD has, at minimum, represented the performance of MEXT in the best light possible. We can’t do a full analysis without knowing how the tests were run, however.What is interesting is AMD’s cautious approach to rolling out MEXT. It’s an EPYC-exclusive feature right now, though AMD left the door open for support on future products (consumer devices, such as Strix Halo) far down the road. It will be sold as a license, bundled with the RAM View software, but we don’t have a timeline on when that will happen. And, despite a partnership with HPE to push out “MEXT Ready” servers, we still don’t know when MEXT itself will be ready for deployment beyond AMD’s walls.Given that conservative approach, there are likely pitfalls to MEXT that we’re not seeing yet, and it’s hard to imagine it will be broadly applicable to every server, at least at the 50% and 25% DRAM capacity levels that AMD showed off with its benchmarks.However, even being able to trim 25% of a server’s DRAM capacity represents a massive cost savings in the current supply-constrained environment. If some workloads can push that to 50% capacity, that’s even better. Of course, we’ll need to see how MEXT holds up once it’s available broadly, but if AMD’s claims hold water, it could become a defining technology in data centers that can’t seem to get enough memory.

items.titleZh: AMD分享如何仅用一半DRAM保持95%服务器性能，借助MEXT规避内存短缺
items.descriptionZh:
AMD已接手名为MEXT的预测式内存引擎技术。MEXT宣称，在仅配置相当于完整DRAM容量25%的物理DIMM时，仍可提供完整DRAM系统99%以上的性能。其核心思路是把“冷”内存页卸载到相对廉价的闪存中，并利用AI模型预测页面需求、提前取回，从而让操作系统仍将缺失的容量视为已安装DRAM。AMD计划明年将这项技术扩展到更广泛的IT基础设施中。

背景上，AI驱动的DRAM价格和供应压力正在影响企业级市场，即使不运行AI负载的企业也受到内存涨价波及。若MEXT能够兑现承诺，在当前供应受限环境下可能具有变革意义。根据AMD和MEXT创始人Gary Smerdon的说法，MEXT可根据应用和性能目标将服务器所需物理DRAM减少20%至75%。在AMD内部部分工作负载中，例如Synopsys PrimeTime，MEXT在50%DRAM容量下可达到完整服务器95%的性能。AMD已在145台服务器内部部署MEXT，并计划明年扩大到2000台；同时宣布与HPE合作，将MEXT推向客户。目前处于推广第一阶段：部分EPYC Venice服务器带有“MEXT Ready”标识，并配备用于卸载的专用NVMe驱动器或插槽。第二阶段将向这些服务器提供MEXT许可证以及RAM View应用，但AMD尚未公布第二阶段时间表。

技术原理上，MEXT的基本流程是：冷页面写入闪存，AI在需要时将这些页面带回，使系统表现得像内存从未缺失。难点在于闪存比DRAM慢几个数量级，按需从闪存流式取回页面通常不可行。MEXT的关键是用AI模型预测将要访问的页面；只要模型预测能比SSD传输延迟提前足够时间，效果就近似于物理DRAM一直存在。MEXT使用基于Transformer的大语言模型，其底层概念与LLM的“下一token预测”类似，只不过MEXT预测的是“下一页”而不是“下一个词”。内存卸载到闪存并非全新概念，但MEXT认为AI是决定性差异。MEXT以Linux内核模块形式部署，可配合任何Linux发行版使用，采用“AI模型集成”，由主Transformer LLM驱动。它不需要预训练：首次部署时在一秒内完成训练，仅占用一个EPYC核心且无需GPU，并随工作负载持续训练，以学习应用的访问模式。

MEXT并不追求在所有场景下完美，也不需要完美。例如，页面存储顺序并不重要，只要所需页面在需要时位于DRAM即可。为帮助理解不同工作负载的适用性，AMD开发了RAM View内存利用工具，可显示哪些页面是热页、哪些已变冷。AMD给出的示例中，一台1.5TB内存系统在整个工作负载下接近满利用率，但任意时刻约有一半内存页面已至少五分钟未被访问；不过AMD未说明该示例的具体工作负载，因此实际冷热分布会因应用而异。AMD最初将MEXT用于内部关键EDA应用，如Synopsys PrimeTime，同时也在优化代理式AI、数据库、媒体和娱乐等负载。

性能数据方面，AMD公布的首方结果看起来亮眼，但测试细节和脚注尚未完整披露，仍需谨慎看待。PrimeTime在50%容量下保留95%性能，在25%容量下仍保留80%性能。在一个Azure三节点集群、第五代EPYC CPU、TPC-DS基准的Spark SQL工作负载中，AMD称MEXT在50%DRAM容量下可达到完整集群99%的性能。代理式AI方面，在五个代理并发的几何平均值下，50%内存容量可达到完整服务器99%的性能，25%容量可达到85%；对于“内存饥渴型”代理，50%和25%容量分别可达到90%和88%的性能。SQL数据库通常会尽量缓存数据以避免I/O瓶颈，这为MEXT释放冷页面提供了机会。

影响和应用场景上，MEXT当前主要面向EPYC服务器，属于较窄的初期应用，但AMD称正在扩展工作负载并取得有希望的早期结果。AMD将MEXT视为延伸“内存墙”的手段：许多工作负载可减少约20%至25%的容量，而减少幅度越大，应用越专用、性能差距也越明显。当前MEXT是EPYC独占功能，AMD未排除未来支持消费级产品（如Strix Halo）的可能，但称那还很遥远。MEXT将以许可证形式销售并捆绑RAM View，但上市时间未定；尽管有HPE合作推出“MEXT Ready”服务器，MEXT本身何时能在AMD之外广泛部署仍不清楚。AMD的保守推进表明该技术可能仍有未显现的陷阱，也难以想象它能适用于所有服务器，尤其是在50%和25%DRAM容量这样的激进水平上。不过，在当前内存供应紧张的环境下，哪怕只削减25%的DRAM容量也意味着显著成本节省；若部分工作负载能推进到50%，收益更大。最终仍需在MEXT广泛可用后验证AMD的说法，但如果这些性能主张成立，它可能成为内存不足的数据中心中的一项关键定义性技术。

items.title: Elon Musk wants to build a s $24 billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Texas company town
items.description: The city of Starbase, Texas, is set to vote on a proposed $24 billion data center to be built within its limits, but the SpaceX company town may not provide the friendly regulatory environment that owner Elon Musk might have hoped for.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Starbase, Texas, which hosts SpaceX’s Starship rocket program, has just posted a notice of a public hearing for a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility within the corporate limits of the city. The project has an initial cost of $24 billion and will apparently be owned by SpaceX. Bloomberg reports that the project could face resistance from incoming Texas governor Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned against approving new data centers until the state's legislature has enacted stronger protections against potential harms from those projects.Until now, Elon Musk's SpaceXSI has been building out its Colossus I and Colossus II data centers near the Mississippi-Tennessee border, but those projects have faced backlash, attracting a lawsuit from area residents that aims to curb the pollutants produced by the large number of gas turbines required to power those facilities.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleNow, it seems that SpaceXSI wants to build another site in Texas that would lie in a city that mostly sits on land owned by SpaceX and whose population mostly comprises its own employees. The project might face reduced local opposition compared to the company's Memphis facilities, as Starbase is essentially a company town for SpaceX. But Hinojosa's arrival in the governor's office could trump that seemingly permissible local regulatory climate.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The project would seem to be a part of SpaceX’s push to build 10 gigawatts of compute in 2027 alone, and the $24 billion budget for this new facility could make it one of the biggest and most expensive data center projects focused on a single site. The company's announcement also notes that the $24 billion outlay it foresees was only for the “initial phases of the projects” and that it could “include future expansions.” That suggests that SpaceXSI could invest in more capacity in Starbase, Texas, going forward, assuming the favorable regulatory climate the company likely hoped for in the area holds.Beyond its new terrestrial ambitions in Starbase, SpaceX also remains hard at work on launching data centers into space. Musk has already laid out the plans for a first-generation AI1 compute satellite with a 150kW peak compute payload, and submitted a proposal to build a 1-million-satellite Orbital Data Center System to the FCC. That work could accelerate after data center measures lost big in the poll in the recent U.S. midterm elections. items.titleZh: 埃隆·马斯克想在得克萨斯州的公司镇建造一台价值240亿美元、由天然气驱动的人工智能超级计算机
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware报道称，位于得克萨斯州的Starbase市已就市界内建设一座燃气发电厂和超级计算设施发布公开听证通知。Starbase是SpaceX“星舰”火箭项目所在地，该项目初始成本为240亿美元，且显然将由SpaceX拥有。背景是，SpaceX此前在密西西比州与田纳西州边界附近建设Colossus I和Colossus II数据中心，因大量燃气轮机供电带来的污染物问题遭到当地居民反对并引发诉讼。Starbase实质上接近SpaceX的“公司镇”：城市大部分土地由SpaceX拥有，人口也主要是公司员工，因此当地反对声可能小于孟菲斯附近项目；但即将上任的得州州长Gina Hinojosa曾主张，在州议会通过更强保护措施以应对数据中心潜在危害之前，不应批准新的数据中心，这可能成为项目阻力。

从技术路径看，该项目把燃气发电与AI超级计算/数据中心设施捆绑，以现场发电满足大规模GPU集群的电力需求。燃气轮机既是供电核心，也是排放和诉讼焦点；SpaceX已开始自制涡轮叶片，以提高燃气发电机输出，体现其在能源设备上的垂直整合。该项目被视为SpaceX“2027年建成10吉瓦算力”计划的一部分，240亿美元仅覆盖“初始阶段”，未来还可能扩建，因而可能成为全球最大、最昂贵的单点数据中心项目之一。相关报道还称，SpaceX的AI业务（文中写作SpaceXAI/SpaceXSI）今年将新增66万块AI GPU，总运营量接近144万块；分析师认为，其在1.5年内建成超过谷歌整个生命周期容量的数据中心算力是可能的。这些参数显示其算力扩张速度和规模远超传统云厂商节奏。

影响层面，地面项目仍面临电力供给、环保审批、选址和社区诉讼等风险。与此同时，SpaceX也在推进太空数据中心：马斯克已公布首代AI1算力卫星，单星峰值算力载荷为150千瓦，并向美国联邦通信委员会提交了由100万颗卫星组成的轨道数据中心系统提案。美国中期选举中数据中心相关措施受挫后，马斯克在X上称“太空数据中心现在看起来很有吸引力”。太空方案可绕开部分地面土地、电力和环保审批瓶颈，但受发射成本、轨道供电与散热、通信带宽、维护及空间监管制约。若相关计划落地，将服务于AI训练和推理等大规模算力需求，并可能改变数据中心的选址、供能和部署模式。

items.title: Ukrainian drone operations squeezed by fiber optic cable shortage triggered by AI data center buildouts
items.description: Ukrainian drone manufacturer BlueBird Tech says that limited fiber optic supplies are making it harder to build jam-proof fiber optic drones.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine sparked a new era of drone warfare. Russian invaders first used drones with fiber-optic tethers to combat electronic warfare on the front lines, but both sides now use these jam-proof drones. Against that backdrop, the AI data center buildout is making it harder for Ukraine to buy the fiber-optic spools that it needs to continue scaling its drone manufacturing capabilities. A research and development representative for BlueBird Tech, a Ukrainian defense firm specializing in drones, told Ars Technica in an interview that prices of fiber optic cables have risen around six to 10 times in the past couple of years as AI data center demand soaks up more and more of the supply of this resource.According to that interview, It’s estimated that Ukraine and Russia are producing around 50,000 fiber optic drones monthly, with each drone capable of ranges of up to 62 miles. But Ukraine has only been able to acquire 72 miles of fiber optic cable from Chinese suppliers during August 2025, whereas Russia imported a whopping 328,000 miles during that same month. It was estimated that Russia acquired 37 million miles of fiber during the entirety of 2025, accounting for over 10% of the global production.What makes matters worse for Ukrainian defenders is that there is an estimated 111-million-mile shortfall in fiber optic cable supply across the world, adding to the various shortages that the data center industry has faced in recent years. Aside from the material shortfall, Ukraine faces trade barriers in acquiring more fiber. The BlueBird representative claimed that some Chinese companies have outright refused to sell Ukraine fiber optic cables.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: China is the primary supplier of this material, so it’s easier for Russia to obtain them through its massive land border with the country. While Ukraine could purchase fiber optic cables from suppliers located in other countries, that's not much of an alternative. The BlueBird rep notes: "there can be intermediaries in other countries, and prices can differ depending on the country and the purchasing route. But in the end, China remains the main source of the fiber optic material we are talking about.”There has also been talk of producing fiber optic cables domestically in Ukraine, but such manufacturing requires specially trained personnel who must practice on the already limited supply of fiber optic cables. Even if manufacturers automate production, they still require experienced personnel who can oversee the line and ensure the quality of the final product. You may like Ukrainian drones hit Russian data centers, disrupting Russian apps and services Russia bombs Ukrainian data centers in latest escalation Ukrainian drone attacks hammer Russia's finance ministry data center, damaged facility reportedly holds tax databases The data center build out has been causing all kinds of shortages. We’ve seen supply shortfalls in GPUs, memory chips, and even PCBs, but there’s also shortages in other seemingly unrelated industries like power infrastructure, optical transceivers, and even in critical skilled labor like electricians. This overwhelming demand has started affecting other industries not related to computing, like cars, home construction, and now, fiber optic attack drones. items.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机行动因AI数据中心建设潮引发光纤短缺而受限
items.descriptionZh:
2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰后，无人机战争进入新阶段。俄军率先在前线使用带光纤系留的无人机来对抗电子战，如今乌俄双方都在使用这种“抗干扰”无人机。其核心原理是用物理光纤替代无线电链路，由地面站通过光纤线轴向无人机传输控制信号和视频回传，从而避免无线电信号被干扰、压制或侦测。相比传统无线电无人机，光纤无人机在强电子战环境下稳定性更高，但代价是需要消耗大量光纤线缆，且线缆供应、成本和后勤保障成为规模化生产的关键瓶颈。

在这一背景下，AI数据中心建设正在加剧乌克兰获取光纤线轴的难度。乌克兰国防无人机企业BlueBird Tech的研发代表在接受Ars Technica采访时称，过去几年光纤电缆价格上涨约6至10倍，原因是AI数据中心对光纤资源的需求不断吞噬供应。据采访估计，乌克兰和俄罗斯每月生产约5万架光纤无人机，每架无人机射程可达62英里（约100公里）。但供应链对比悬殊：2025年8月，乌克兰仅从中国供应商获得72英里光纤电缆，而俄罗斯同月进口高达32.8万英里；据估计，俄罗斯2025年全年获得约3700万英里光纤，占全球产量超过10%。

更不利的是，全球光纤电缆供应估计存在1.11亿英里缺口，这进一步加剧了数据中心行业近年遭遇的多类短缺。除材料不足外，乌克兰还面临贸易壁垒。BlueBird代表称，一些中国公司直接拒绝向乌克兰出售光纤电缆。中国是该材料的主要供应国，俄罗斯凭借与中国的漫长陆地边界更容易获得供应。乌克兰虽可从其他国家供应商采购，但替代方案有限。该代表表示，其他国家可能存在中间商，价格会因国家和采购路线不同而变化，“但归根结底，中国仍是我们所说的光纤材料的主要来源”。

乌克兰也在讨论本土生产光纤电缆，但制造需要经过专门培训的人员，而培训又必须在已经有限的光纤供应上练习。即使实现自动化生产，仍需要经验丰富的人员监督生产线并确保最终产品质量。文章还指出，数据中心建设潮已造成GPU、内存芯片、PCB，以及电力基础设施、光收发器甚至电工等关键熟练劳动力短缺。这种巨大需求正开始影响与计算无关的行业，如汽车、住宅建设，如今又波及光纤攻击无人机。对乌克兰而言，AI数据中心对光纤资源的争夺不仅推高价格，还通过全球供应短缺和采购壁垒削弱其继续扩大光纤无人机制造能力的前景。

history.title: Nvidia’s Board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang as second extra-marital affair emerges
history.description: Nvidia Board reportedly moves to expel Jensen Huang as stock tumbles on latest scandals and lack of succession plans at Nvidia.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia's Board of Directors is preparing to oust co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang following revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence and another with an Nvidia executive, reports The Wall Street Journal. Although no final decision has been made yet, the company's directors could meet as early as November 11 to discuss Huang's future. Whoever succeeds Huang will be the company's second CEO in 33 years. Nvidia's stock dropped 8% in after-hours trading following the reports. Nvidia's board of directors launched an independent investigation into the matter on November 8.The report from the WSJ comes hours after the New York Times revealed that Huang allegedly had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. According to five people who worked at Nvidia, the relationship was known internally, while Huang and Powell were reportedly seen together at a San Jose hotel during Nvidia's GTC conference in March. The allegations follow an earlier report that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese intelligence asset.A similar controversy cost Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich his position in June 2018, when an internal investigation confirmed that he had maintained a consensual relationship with an employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers. It is noteworthy that Nvidia's code of conduct explicitly identifies personal relationships as potential conflicts of interest and instructs employees to consult the company's legal department when such conflicts arise. Whether Huang violated Nvidia's internal policies remains unclear, as the code of conduct does not explicitly prohibit all relationships between managers and subordinates.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Huang's potential departure would mark the first CEO transition in Nvidia's 33-year history, and therefore his succession has become an immediate concern for Nvidia, which does not have anyone of Huang's caliber in the leadership team. Although chief financial officer Colette Kress could potentially serve as interim chief executive if Huang is ousted while the BoD searches for a permanent replacement, it remains to be seen how Wall Street would react to this assignment.Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky, who used to be the company's senior vice president of engineering and operations and remains a member of the company's board and an Nvidia Fellow, could also play a role in the succession process, given his extensive knowledge of Nvidia's technology, corporate culture, and history. However, has not served in an executive role at Nvidia for at least a decade, so the chances that he will succeed Huang are low. history.titleZh: 英伟达董事会据报准备罢免CEO黄仁勋，第二段婚外情曝光
history.descriptionZh:
据Tom's Hardware报道，英伟达董事会正筹备罢免联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋（Jensen Huang），起因是《华尔街日报》披露其存在两段婚外情：一段涉及一名被怀疑为中国情报机构工作的女性，另一段涉及英伟达内部一名直接向他汇报的高管。董事会尚未作出最终决定，但最早可能于11月11日召开会议讨论黄仁勋的去留。若黄仁勋离任，继任者将成为英伟达33年历史上第二位CEO。消息传出后，英伟达股价在盘后交易中下跌8%。董事会已于11月8日就此启动独立调查。

在《华尔街日报》报道前数小时，《纽约时报》称黄仁勋与英伟达医疗健康业务副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔（Kimberly Powell）存在婚外情，鲍威尔直接向黄仁勋汇报。五名曾在英伟达工作的知情人士称，这段关系在公司内部广为人知；据称今年3月英伟达GTC大会期间，两人曾在圣何塞一家酒店一同出现。此前还有报道称，黄仁勋与一名叫Alice Huang的华裔女商人存在关系，美国情报部门认为此人是中国情报资产。

这一风波与英特尔前CEO布莱恩·科再奇（Brian Krzanich）2018年6月的遭遇相似：当时英特尔内部调查确认科再奇与一名员工保持双方自愿的恋爱关系，违反了适用于所有管理者的禁止亲密关系政策，科再奇因此辞职。值得注意的是，英伟达的行为准则明确将私人关系列为潜在利益冲突，并指示员工在出现此类冲突时咨询公司法务部门。但由于准则并未明确禁止管理者与下属之间的一切恋爱关系，黄仁勋是否违反英伟达内部政策目前仍不清楚。

黄仁勋可能的离任将标志英伟达33年来首次CEO更替，继任问题因此成为公司当务之急，而英伟达领导团队中并无与黄仁勋同等量级的人物。若黄仁勋被罢免，首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）可能在董事会寻找正式继任者期间出任临时CEO，但华尔街对这一安排的反映尚待观察。英伟达联合创始人克里斯·马拉科夫斯基（Chris Malachowsky）也可能在继任过程中发挥作用——他曾任公司工程与运营高级副总裁，目前仍是董事会成员和英伟达院士（Nvidia Fellow），对公司的技术、企业文化和历史有深入了解；但他已至少十年未在英伟达担任高管职务，因此接替黄仁勋的可能性较低。此前周日，董事们曾对黄仁勋及其领导团队表达信心，但这一措辞并不足以保证其继续留任。

整体来看，此事的核心影响集中在公司治理与领导层稳定性层面：一方面，英伟达的行为准则与英特尔此前的处理先例，为董事会评估高管私人关系是否构成利益冲突提供了参照；另一方面，由于黄仁勋长期是英伟达战略与技术路线的核心人物，其去留的不确定性可能波及投资者信心、公司战略延续性以及华尔街对英伟达管理层的评估。

history.titleZh: 据报道英伟达正准备解雇黄仁勋
history.descriptionZh:
据《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达董事会正准备罢免CEO黄仁勋。此前《纽约时报》称，黄仁勋被指涉及第二段婚外情；而就在几天前，他才承认与一名据称是中国间谍的女性、Megaspeed高管Alice Huang存在婚外关系。报道称，第二段涉嫌婚外情的对象是直接向黄仁勋汇报的英伟达医疗保健业务副总裁Kimberly Powell。《华尔街日报》称，英伟达董事会最快将于今天开会，决定黄仁勋在公司内的去留。英伟达未立即回应The Verge的置评请求。

《纽约时报》援引两名匿名消息人士称，黄仁勋与Powell均已婚，二人据称于今年3月英伟达GTC开发者大会期间在圣何塞一家酒店被拍到一起；但《纽约时报》表示尚未看到相关视频。CNBC援引一名匿名消息人士称，有关两人关系的传闻在英伟达内部已流传很久，部分原因是Powell没有医疗健康或科学背景。受消息影响，英伟达股价周三盘后下跌超过7%。

背景方面，英伟达和黄仁勋在周末确认了与Megaspeed高管、据称间谍Alice Huang的婚外关系，并启动后续调查。公司表示已聘请前美国联邦检察官Joon H. Kim及其所在的Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz律所处理此事。但最新传闻显示，董事会可能不会等待调查结果就采取行动。Wired报道称，黄仁勋去年还聘请了以处理公开性丑闻著称的危机公关公司Heller；该公司创始人曾为面临公众审视的多位权势人物提供建议，包括前国会议员Anthony Weiner和作家Jeffrey Toobin。Heller未立即回应The Verge的置评请求。

这篇新闻本身不涉及英伟达芯片技术发布或性能参数，核心是公司治理、高管风险和领导层不确定性。英伟达当前在AI加速芯片市场占据主导地位，其GPU和CUDA生态是全球AI训练与推理基础设施的关键。若CEO突然更迭，市场关注点将集中在董事会决策的合法性、继任安排、战略连续性以及对Blackwell等下一代AI芯片路线、客户关系和供应链的影响。盘后7%以上的跌幅已反映投资者对治理风险的即时担忧。不过，相关婚外情和“间谍”指控目前均来自媒体报道和匿名消息人士，部分内容仍有待证实；英伟达董事会最终是否罢免黄仁勋，以及调查结果如何，仍需后续确认。

history.title: OpenAI and Georgia county leaders hit with Mafia-style RICO racketeering lawsuit over $30 billion AI data center
history.description: The plaintiffs alleged that the parties committed fraud and concealment through NDAs and misleading public statements.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Residents of Effingham County, Georgia, just filed a RICO lawsuit against their county commissioners, county leaders, and OpenAI and its affiliates, alleging that they committed various offenses in a conspiracy to get OpenAI’s “Project Camellia” approved. According to the Effingham Herald, the plaintiffs — Dr. Michelle Finch-Mincey, Lehman Mincey Jr., and Raymond Carver — are seeking civil damages, saying that the project has harmed their property values and even pointing out that purchase offers for nearby residential properties have dropped or been withdrawn since the data center was announced.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe lawsuit names all Effingham County Commissioners — Chairperson Damon Rahn, Forrest Floyd, Roger Burdette, Jamie DeLoach, Elizabeth Helmly, and Phil Kieffer — as defendants, alongside County Manager Tim Callanan, Effingham County Industrial Development Authority (IDA) CEO Brandt Herndon, the IDA itself, OpenAI, Octans GA LLC, the entity operating the data center on behalf of OpenAI, and Savannah Industrial Development LLC, the agency involved in the sale of IDA property to Octans and OpenAI.It’s alleged that the defendants committed fraud and concealment through non-disclosure agreements and misleading public statements so that residents remain unaware of the nature of the projects for as long as possible, and that there was a civil conspiracy “to advance Project Camellia through confidential negotiations and closed-door decisions.” They also claimed that the parties engaged in improper land transactions, zoning violations, and civil racketeering.wLatest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Project Camellia is one of OpenAI’s biggest data center projects planned for construction in Effingham County. The site is expected to cost somewhere between $20 billion and $30 billion, to be built across five phases, with a planned compute capacity of 3.2 gigawatts. The company also promised that it will not affect the community’s utility costs, as it will pay for the full cost of all its required infrastructure upgrades, and that it will have minimal water use due to its closed-loop water system. Despite those promises, it seems that some people are opposing the project because of how the county had allegedly tried to secure the land, tax incentives, and zoning approvals without informing the residents until key decisions were finalized and contracts had been signed.The RICO Act — or Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act — was originally conceived as a way to counter organized crime, particularly Mafia leadership, who often used low-level members to commit individual crimes and do the dirty work for them. However, Georgia’s RICO Act is less stringent than the federal version, which is why it’s been used multiple times for cases that seemingly had nothing to do with the Mafia. For example, it was in the 2023 election racketeering case against Donald Trump and 18 others in the attempt to overturn the 2020 U.S. presidential election results in the state, and it was also used in Young Thug’s trial after the rapper was accused of running YSL Records as a criminal street gang. You may like Local opposition blocked $68 billion worth of data center projects in the second quarter of 2026 OpenAI considers rebranding data centers to 'AI compute campuses" as data center backlash intensifies Microsoft-backed AI data center faces backlash over alleged unpermitted gas turbines and 1.5M-gallon LNG tank Critics say that Georgia’s version is way too encompassing, though, and that it was being used to squeeze defendants involved in more mundane or common felonies. “When you have a hammer, everything looks like a nail,” Georgia State University professor of criminal justice and criminology Volkan Topalli said in Atlanta Magazine.The actions of both state officials, OpenAI, and its affiliates are not new, though. There have already been multiple complaints of data center developers and local governments using non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) while they negotiate terms for possible data center projects. Developers say they use this tool to avoid “running afoul of insider trading rules,” but people have pointed out that West Feliciana Parish in Louisiana was able to close a data center deal without resorting to one. An AWS data center in Gilroy, California, is also facing scrutiny after residents only discovered the nature of the project when construction began after a five-year permitting saga that relied on zoning rules that were set 45 years ago.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

history.titleZh: OpenAI和佐治亚州县领导因300亿美元AI数据中心遭遇黑手党式RICO敲诈勒索诉讼
history.descriptionZh:
据《Effingham Herald》和Tom's Hardware报道，美国佐治亚州埃芬汉县居民Michelle Finch-Mincey博士、Lehman Mincey Jr.和Raymond Carver已依据佐治亚州《反诈骗及腐败组织法》（RICO）提起诉讼，控告县委员、县领导层以及OpenAI及其关联方在推动OpenAI“Project Camellia”数据中心项目获批过程中涉嫌合谋违法。被告包括全部县委员——主席Damon Rahn，以及Forrest Floyd、Roger Burdette、Jamie DeLoach、Elizabeth Helmly、Phil Kieffer——县经理Tim Callanan、埃芬汉县工业发展局（IDA）及其CEO Brandt Herndon、OpenAI、代表OpenAI运营该数据中心的Octans GA LLC，以及参与IDA向Octans和OpenAI出售土地的Savannah Industrial Development LLC。原告寻求民事赔偿，称项目已损害其房产价值，并指出自数据中心宣布以来，附近住宅的收购报价已经下降或被撤回。

原告的核心指控是：被告通过保密协议（NDA）和误导性公开声明实施欺诈与隐瞒，使居民尽可能长时间不了解项目性质；各方还通过保密谈判和闭门决策推动Project Camellia，涉嫌不当土地交易、违反区划规定和民事敲诈勒索。争议焦点在于，县政府被指在土地、税收优惠和区划审批等关键决策完成、合同签署之前，没有充分告知居民。Project Camellia是OpenAI计划在埃芬汉县建设的最大数据中心项目之一，预计投资200亿至300亿美元，分五期建设，规划算力/电力容量达3.2吉瓦。OpenAI承诺承担全部必要基础设施升级费用，不影响社区公用事业成本，并通过闭环水系统尽量减少用水。技术层面，这不是芯片产品，而是超大规模AI算力基础设施：以吉瓦级电力容量支撑大模型训练和推理，五期滚动建设降低一次性部署风险，闭环水冷则针对数据中心散热和水资源约束；但其治理透明度争议已盖过技术承诺。

RICO原为打击有组织犯罪、尤其是黑手党领导层而设，但佐治亚州版本比联邦版本更宽泛，曾被用于2023年针对特朗普等人的选举敲诈案，以及说唱歌手Young Thug案。批评者认为佐治亚州RICO适用范围过广。此案也折射出AI数据中心选址中的普遍矛盾：开发商和地方政府常用NDA推进谈判，开发商称这是为避免触犯内幕交易规则，但路易斯安那州West Feliciana Parish曾在没有NDA的情况下完成数据中心交易；加州Gilroy的AWS数据中心也因居民直到施工开始才发现项目而受到审视，该案经历了五年许可程序，并依赖45年前制定的区划规则。该诉讼可能影响OpenAI项目推进、当地房产价值和社区关系，并成为AI数据中心选址透明度、公众参与和地方审批程序的重要案例。

history.title: SpaceX develops its own ‘Kessel’ rack-scale system featuring 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for data centers in space, report claims
history.description: SpaceX is reportedly developing a 'Kessel' rack-scale system design with 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs that relies on a massive 84-layer PCB midplane.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter SpaceX/xAI is developing a custom version of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale AI system that replaces conventional NVLink cable assemblies with a massive 84-layer printed circuit board (PCB), in part for use in orbital data centers, reports SemiAnalysis. The system is codenamed Kessel and retains 36 Vera CPUs, 72 Rubin GPUs, and nine NVLink switch trays, but introduces a different solid-state interconnect architecture. While SpaceX/xAI will continue to buy Nvidia hardware directly from the company, Elon Musk's company will source other components independently, which could give it greater control over its hardware supply chain.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCThe Kessel system retains the fundamental configuration of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, which comprises 72 GPU packages distributed across 18 compute trays and nine NVLink switch trays. However, instead of Nvidia's conventional arrangement with internal NVLink cable cartridges, SpaceX plans to position compute and switch trays back-to-back around a passive PCB midplane. The architecture resembles a smaller version of Nvidia's Kyber design with 576 AI GPUs (albeit in 144 packages), which also relies on a PCB-based interconnect rather than conventional cable assemblies, SemiAnalysis notes. Interestingly, the design is aimed at both terrestrial and orbital deployments, according to the analysts.Arguably the most distinctive feature of Kessel is its 84-layer PCB midplane, which uses ultra-low-loss M10 copper-clad laminates (CCLs). By contrast, Nvidia's Kyber architecture relied on a backplane based on a considerably more complex 156-layer PCB featuring M9 CCLs. The reduction in layer count by nearly half could substantially improve manufacturability and production yields, but the more advanced copper-clad laminate will almost certainly increase material costs. In any case, an 84-layer PCB is a device that is exceptionally hard to build.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The move to a PCB midplane could simplify system assembly by eliminating numerous high-speed cable connections, but it would not necessarily reduce manufacturing costs. An 84-layer PCB that relies on ultra-low-loss M10 laminate is an exceptionally expensive component that requires sophisticated manufacturing processes and precise quality control. To put an 84-layer PCB number into context, modern high-end server motherboards use 15 – 20 layers, whereas server development boards use more than 20 layers to virtually eliminate any electrical issues with the board itself. Furthermore, manufacturing yields of an 84-layer PCB could become a major obstacle, as defects in internal layers may render an entire board unusable. Consequently, the economic viability of Kessel will depend on whether savings from cable elimination and independent component procurement can offset the cost of its complex midplane.Perhaps more importantly, Kessel represents a departure from Nvidia's conventional system-level procurement model. Instead of purchasing Nvidia's assembled L6 compute boards or even L10 trays that Nvidia plans to sell with its Vera Rubin generation, SpaceX reportedly plans to acquire AI accelerators, CPUs, switches, and networking components directly from Nvidia and procure other components from third-party suppliers (one can wonder how easy it will be for SpaceX/xAI to procure memory amid today's shortages). This would enable SpaceX to select its own PCB manufacturers, component vendors, and manufacturing partners, optimize its hardware for its infrastructure (which will be important for orbital deployments), and perhaps reduce intermediary costs. Meanwhile, the company would assume greater responsibility for system design, validation, manufacturing quality, and supply-chain management, which is something that most hyperscalers have been doing in recent years. You may like SpaceX reportedly seeking $40 billion debt package for Nvidia AI hardware SpaceXAI will deploy standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs for Grok's agentic workloads Chinese AI lab Moonshot reportedly looked at European data centers to access Nvidia chips, report claims For Nvidia, the implications are less straightforward. Although direct sales of CPU and AI GPU packages could reduce the company's revenue from complete compute-board assemblies, the arrangement could also encourage other large customers to develop their own Nvidia-based systems and eventually deploy more Nvidia-based machines, something that may be important in a world where custom silicon developed by hyperscalers is rapidly gaining traction. However, to make this happen, Kessel must be a smashing success that will offer clear advantages over systems designed by Nvidia. history.titleZh: 报道称，SpaceX 开发出自有的“Kessel”机架级系统，搭载 72
history.descriptionZh:
据 SemiAnalysis 报道，SpaceX/xAI 正在开发英伟达 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架级 AI 系统的定制版本，代号 Kessel。该系统最大的变化是用一块大型 84 层印制电路板（PCB）中板替代传统的 NVLink 线缆组件，并计划同时面向地面和轨道数据中心部署。Kessel 仍保留 Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 的基本配置：36 颗 Vera CPU、72 颗 Rubin GPU，以及 9 个 NVLink 交换机托盘；72 个 GPU 封装分布在 18 个计算托盘和 9 个交换机托盘上。不同之处在于，SpaceX 计划把计算托盘和交换机托盘背靠背布置在一块无源 PCB 中板周围，而不是采用 Nvidia 常规的内部 NVLink 线缆盒。这一架构类似 Nvidia Kyber 设计的缩小版：Kyber 面向 576 个 AI GPU（144 个封装），同样依赖 PCB 互连而非传统线缆组件。

Kessel 最引人注目的特点是其 84 层 PCB 中板，采用超低损耗 M10 覆铜板（CCL）。作为对比，Nvidia Kyber 使用的是更复杂的 156 层 PCB 背板，搭配 M9 CCL。将层数减少近一半，可能显著改善可制造性和生产良率，但更先进的覆铜板几乎必然会提高材料成本。84 层 PCB 本身也是极难制造的器件。转向 PCB 中板可以简化系统组装，消除大量高速线缆连接，但并不必然降低制造成本：超低损耗 M10 层压板非常昂贵，需要复杂制造工艺和精确质量控制。作为参照，现代高端服务器主板通常使用 15—20 层，服务器开发板使用 20 层以上以尽量避免板级电气问题。84 层 PCB 的良率可能成为主要障碍，因为内部层缺陷可能导致整块板报废。因此，Kessel 的经济可行性取决于取消线缆和独立采购组件带来的节省，能否抵消复杂中板的成本。

更重要的是，Kessel 偏离了 Nvidia 传统的系统级采购模式。SpaceX 据称不购买 Nvidia 组装的 L6 计算板，也不购买 Nvidia 计划随 Vera Rubin 一代销售的 L10 托盘，而是直接从 Nvidia 采购 AI 加速器、CPU、交换机和网络组件，并从第三方供应商采购其他组件。在当前内存供应紧张的背景下，SpaceX/xAI 如何采购内存也值得关注。这种模式使 SpaceX 可以选择自己的 PCB 制造商、组件供应商和制造伙伴，针对自身基础设施优化硬件，这对轨道部署尤为重要，并可能降低中间成本。但与此同时，SpaceX 将承担更多系统设计、验证、制造质量和供应链管理责任，这也是近年来多数超大规模云厂商正在做的事情。

对 Nvidia 而言，影响并不简单。直接销售 CPU 和 AI GPU 封装可能减少其来自完整计算板组件的收入，但这种安排也可能鼓励其他大客户开发基于 Nvidia 的自有系统，最终部署更多 Nvidia 机器。在超大规模厂商自研芯片迅速崛起的背景下，这一点可能很重要。不过，Kessel 必须取得显著成功，并相比 Nvidia 设计的系统展现出明确优势，这一模式才可能真正推广。

history.title: Softbank loses $3.7 billion on canceled AI data center gas turbine orders days after denying Elon Musk’s claim it was defaulting
history.description: SoftBank might not have defaulted on a raft of gas turbine orders, but it has pulled out of deals for unwanted power units after overestimating how many it could use amid the AI data center buildout boom.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter By early 2026, Japanese tech investment outfit SoftBank had reserved more power generation capacity than the entire state of Connecticut after cornering a huge portion of the global gas turbine production capacity. Now, the same company has chosen to take a $3.7 billion hit to its earnings after canceling reservations for the highly sought-after power generation hardware. The WSJ reports that SoftBank had reserved more than 13 gigawatts of power-producing turbines, citing unnamed "people familiar with the orders." That's the equivalent of more than six Hoover Dams' worth of capacity, with SoftBank founder and chief executive Masayoshi Son believing that it would be vital to the company's earning potential moving forward. Notably, this development surfaced after SoftBank's CFO fired back at Elon Musk's recent revelation that the company had defaulted on turbine blade contracts, saying, "there is no such default."Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThe gas turbines were to power AI data centers, and SoftBank is set to build a 9.2-gigawatt power plant in Ohio, with construction scheduled for early 2027. It'll cost $33 billion to build and will provide power to a neighboring eight-gigawatt data center. That data center will be leased to OpenAI, albeit only after Nvidia entered discussions about guaranteeing around $250 billion of financing for the project.But SoftBank got ahead of itself. After initially planning to use the turbines for future gas-powered plants, the company has now chosen to change direction. Orders for turbines, engines that convert natural gas into the electricity used by data centers, must be placed years in advance of them being required. The company had bet big, placing huge orders with the expectation that demand would greatly outstrip supply. That would leave SoftBank in an enviable position, holding huge orders for the vital components required as part of a data center rollout boosted by AI demand. But those reservations weren't cheap — turbine manufacturers regularly charge customers tens of millions of dollars per gigawatt.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: It's now canceled its remaining reservations with GE Vernova, its turbine supplier, while also unwinding contracts for orders that were too far gone. SoftBank told investors on a recent earnings call that the orders had been placed “to secure power generation equipment in anticipation of shortages,” but it now appears it anticipated a little too much.Crucially, SoftBank is also keen for everyone to know that this move was voluntary and that it did not default on its orders. That's contrary to what xAI CEO Elon Musk claimed in a post on his X social network. history.titleZh: 软银因AI数据中心燃气轮机订单被取消损失37亿美元，就在其否认埃隆·马斯克称其违约的几天后
history.descriptionZh:
日本科技投资集团软银在AI数据中心电力需求激增的背景下，曾大举锁定燃气轮机产能：到2026年初，其预留的发电容量甚至超过美国康涅狄格州全州发电能力，并拿下全球燃气轮机产能的很大一部分。据《华尔街日报》报道，软银预留了超过13GW的燃气发电轮机，相当于六个以上胡佛水坝的装机容量。软银创始人兼CEO孙正义认为，这些稀缺设备对公司的未来盈利潜力至关重要。燃气轮机将天然气转化为电能，是数据中心自备电站或并网电站的核心设备；由于制造周期长，相关订单通常需要提前数年下达。软银原本押注AI带来的电力需求将远超供给，因此提前锁定关键设备，希望在未来数据中心建设中占据有利位置。但这类预留并不便宜，轮机制造商通常按每GW数千万美元向客户收费。

如今，软银选择取消剩余预留，并对业绩计入37亿美元冲击。公司取消了向燃气轮机制造商GE Vernova的剩余订单，同时解除了一些“已经推进过远”的合同。软银在近期财报电话会上告诉投资者，这些订单是为了“预判短缺而确保发电设备”，但现在看显然预期过高。相关项目包括在俄亥俄州建设一座9.2GW燃气电站，计划2027年初开工，造价330亿美元，并为邻近一座8GW数据中心供电。该数据中心拟租给OpenAI，但前提包括英伟达就约2500亿美元融资担保进行讨论。软银还特别强调，此次取消是自愿行为，并非违约；公司CFO后藤芳光否认了马斯克在X上所称软银违约涡轮叶片合同的说法，称“这完全不对，不存在这样的违约”。

从技术影响看，AI基础设施的瓶颈正从芯片扩展到电力。燃气发电能够提供稳定基荷电力，并相对可控地快速部署，适合支撑大规模AI数据中心，但需要提前锁定产能、承担巨额资本开支，并面对排放和监管约束。软银的撤退表明，即便AI电力需求长期看涨，提前数年超额预订关键设备也会带来财务和履约风险；同时，电力供应、融资担保和大客户租约正成为AI数据中心能否落地的核心变量。

history.title: ASRock quietly rolls out new firmware after disastrous previous update killed Radeon RX 7900-series GPUs
history.description: Asrock's VBIOS 1.0.6 update follows reports of Radeon RX 7900 XT and XTX graphics cards failing to boot after installing the previous firmware.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter ASRock has rolled out a new firmware update for its Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards. The latest VBIOS version 1.0.6 appears to be a follow-up to the previous 1.0.5 release. According to community reports, that older version was bricking some of the company's Radeon RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX graphics cards. The new update has now quietly made its way to the ASRock official website, although the company has not published a changelog or provided any details on what the new update addresses.Last month, AMD released a VBIOS patch for Radeon RX 7000-series graphics cards to address potential security vulnerabilities. While the company did not disclose any technical details about the vulnerabilities, it assured gamers that there had been no reports of them being exploited. According to a statement shared with ComputerBase, the company provided the following rationale for the update:Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PC"AMD is releasing a firmware update as part of our usual approach to address potential security vulnerabilities. These corrections are already made available before the public announcement to give customers time to update their firmware. As a best practice, we recommend that users update the firmware of their graphics cards as soon as they are provided by the respective GPU manufacturer. There are no reports of exploiting these security vulnerabilities in practice."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: ASRock subsequently listed the 1.0.5 VBIOS update for 10 graphics card models, spanning its Radeon RX 7600 XT, RX 7700 XT, RX 7800 XT, RX 7900 XT, and RX 7900 XTX families. However, several Radeon RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX owners reported that their systems failed to boot after installing the firmware. Some lucky users were able to use external EEPROM programmers to recover their cards. Although ASRock has since removed the 1.0.5 update from its website, it has yet to provide clarity on what caused the failures or confirm whether the newly released VBIOS addresses the issue.There are also unanswered questions around how ASRock plans to help customers who have already been affected. According to reports shared with VideoCardz, a user in Japan received a confirmation from ASRock that the failed update would be covered under warranty. However, another owner in Europe was reportedly directed to seek warranty service despite having an out-of-warranty graphics card. This essentially leaves affected owners uncertain of whether they will receive free repairs or replacements. history.titleZh: 华擎在此前灾难性更新导致 Radeon RX 7900 系列 GPU 损坏后悄然推出新固件
history.descriptionZh:
华擎（ASRock）已为其 Radeon RX 7000 系列显卡发布新版 VBIOS 固件 1.0.6，被视为此前 1.0.5 版本的后续更新。事件背景是：社区报告称，华擎此前发布的 1.0.5 VBIOS 导致部分 Radeon RX 7900 XT 和 RX 7900 XTX 显卡无法启动，也就是俗称的“变砖”。新版 1.0.6 已悄然上线华擎官网，但华擎没有发布更新日志，也未说明该版本具体修复了什么问题。

这一轮固件更新的上游背景是 AMD 上月为 Radeon RX 7000 系列发布 VBIOS 补丁，以修复潜在安全漏洞。AMD 未披露漏洞技术细节，但表示没有收到这些漏洞在实际环境中被利用的报告。AMD 在给 ComputerBase 的声明中称，这是其处理潜在安全漏洞的常规做法，相关修正会在公开宣布前提供给客户，以便用户有时间更新固件，并建议用户尽快安装显卡厂商提供的固件更新。

从技术层面看，VBIOS 是显卡的基础固件，负责硬件初始化、供电与频率等底层参数配置，因此固件刷写异常可能导致显卡无法正常点亮。华擎随后曾为 10 款显卡型号列出 1.0.5 VBIOS 更新，覆盖 Radeon RX 7600 XT、RX 7700 XT、RX 7800 XT、RX 7900 XT 和 RX 7900 XTX 系列。但多名 RX 7900 XT 和 RX 7900 XTX 用户报告，安装该固件后系统无法启动；部分用户借助外部 EEPROM 编程器才恢复显卡。华擎已从官网撤下 1.0.5 更新，但尚未说明失败原因，也未确认新发布的 1.0.6 是否解决该问题。

在售后层面，受影响用户的处理方式仍不明确。据报道，一名日本用户获得华擎确认，失败更新将纳入保修范围；但另一名欧洲用户据称被要求走保修服务，而其显卡已过保。这意味着受影响用户仍不确定能否获得免费维修或更换。由于 1.0.6 没有更新日志和官方说明，用户也难以判断安装该替代固件是否安全。原文未提供性能参数或性能对比数据，事件核心并非性能提升，而是安全漏洞修复、固件更新风险及厂商沟通与售后问题。对于游戏玩家和 RX 7000 系列用户而言，是否以及何时安装 1.0.6，目前仍需等待华擎给出更清晰的说明。

history.title: Cognichip reveals how its new AI-assisted program can slash chip design times from months to days — automating labor-intensive tasks cuts design time down, Chief Product Officer explains
history.description: Cognichip claims its AI can slash chip design time from months to days, only that that design must be very simplistic.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Amid the AI gold rush, one particularly fruitful vein of research is the emergence of AI-assisted workflows in electronic design automation (EDA) tools like Cadence Maestro. One such company developing such foundational models is Cognichip, which in September launched Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI), proprietary AI models developed specifically for semiconductor engineering. ACI deploys the 'industry’s largest training dataset' across semiconductor physics and chip design principles.ACI Enterprise is Cognichip's deployable platform, which combines these specialized models with agentic workflows, project memory, and computing infrastructure for AI inference. The company describes ACI's approach as a self-learning flywheel, a continuously evolving design environment that brings together specifications, register-transfer level (RTL), and verification results to build a design that meets power, performance, and area (PPA) targets to Pareto limits. We sat down with Cognichip to learn more."We have surpassed, I think, over ten million training samples in our datasets that are either things that we designed ourselves directly or things that have been generated through our synthetic technology," says Stelios Diamantidis, Chief Product Officer at Cognichip, in an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium. "We have invented new ways of creating synthetic training samples for semiconductor design. And very importantly, now that we have all these data samples, characterized data samples, we also had to invent new models so that we can capture the data, and we also had to invent new pipelines for training so that we can map the training data to the models themselves."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Cognichip)A self-learning flywheelCognichip says ACI can analyze specifications, explore microarchitectural options, generate RTL, verify designs, identify and fix functional problems, and optimize designs to meet PPA targets. The system can also integrate existing IP modules and even produce FPGA implementations. In principle, ACI enables engineers to focus on product requirements and architectural decisions while ACI handles much of the logic implementation and verification work."Build the spec, build the RTL, estimate PPA, perform optimizations, run verification, everything," Diamantidis told us while explaining how ACI can develop and evaluate multiple architectural alternatives before engineers select the preferred design. "We do not try to turn the designer into a verification engine; our system is self-verified, so we want the designer to design, and we want our system not only to do the tasks but also verify them." You may like The state of agentic AI in chip design tools in 2026 ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond Because ACI operates as a self-learning flywheel, Cognichip claims engineers can revisit earlier architectural decisions and modify their designs without restarting the entire development process from scratch."Architecture, microarchitecture, RTL, all abstractions in the cognitive system are aligned, so the change in microarchitecture is essentially automatically reflected in RTL, and vice versa," Diamantidis explained. "Changes in RTL are automatically reflected in microarchitecture."Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsCognichip says it has participated in more than 40 customer engagements, including projects at Renesas and SiTime. According to the company, these engagements span a wide range of chip designs, from microcontrollers and encryption engines to networking processors, RISC-V CPUs, and AI accelerators.To illustrate ACI's capabilities, Cognichip points to an evaluation conducted with an unnamed leading fabless semiconductor company. The customer provided an existing 55-page microarchitecture specification, which ACI used to explore architecture options, develop RTL from scratch, and integrate middleware and other components. The system also generated SystemVerilog testbenches, ran simulations, identified and corrected errors, and achieved functional verification closure with over 90% UVM coverage, the company claims. According to Cognichip, the entire process took just 10 days and required only one engineer. By contrast, doing the same job using conventional methods would require a full front-end design team and approximately 20 weeks, Cognichip says.However, there are several important caveats. First up, the customer had already provided a detailed 55-page microarchitecture specification, so the platform did not begin with a blank sheet. Secondly, Cognichip has not disclosed the complexity of the design, which makes it difficult to assess how much work has been done (or rather, processed). Finally, the reported acceleration applies to front-end engineering rather than the entire chip development process, which also includes physical implementation, tape-out, manufacturing, and silicon validation.Making very educated guesses/predictionsThere is a substantial difference between developing functionally, conducting verified RTL, and prepping a chip design for manufacturing. Although Cognichip's ACI can develop microarchitectures, generate RTL, and optimize designs for PPA, the platform does not perform physical implementation. Tasks such as floorplanning, placement and routing, clock-tree synthesis, physical verification, and signoff still require conventional electronic design automation (EDA) tools from companies like Cadence, Synopsys, and Siemens EDA. What to read next OpenAI Jalapeño design interview transcript OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design Cadence reveals Maestro, fine-tuned AI models built to run specialized chip design agents, with early access coming for 'select customers' in Q4 2026 "Today we do not do physical implementation," Diamantidis said. "So, place and route […] is done outside of our system." (Image credit: Cognichip)This distinction matters because an architecture that meets its estimated PPA targets may fail to achieve them after physical implementation. For example, a design expected to operate at 1 GHz while consuming 15 W could achieve only 800 MHz at 20 W once engineers account for interconnect delays, clock distribution, buffering requirements, congestion, and other physical effects. Such discrepancies can require changes to RTL or even fundamental architectural elements, followed by another round of verification and physical implementation. In some cases, these iterations can consume weeks or months of engineering time."That cycle is very expensive in terms of time," Diamantidis said. "Because you are crossing design boundaries, and you are running very long runtimes and all that."Cognichip claims that ACI can reduce these costly iterations by predicting the physical consequences of architectural decisions before implementation begins. According to Diamantidis, the company has trained its models on internally developed and characterized semiconductor designs, which enables ACI to estimate PPA characteristics and identify potential architectural trade-offs during front-end development."We have trained models with full physical stack visibility understanding so that the models can predict the PPA during the front-end design phase." "We can identify those trade-offs before going to physical implementation."For example, ACI could recommend replacing two independent FIFOs with a single time-multiplexed FIFO to reduce power consumption at the expense of performance. Diamantidis used this hypothetical scenario to illustrate how the platform can evaluate architectural alternatives before engineers commit to a particular implementation."If you want to save power here at the cost of 10% of frequency, take these two FIFOs that you have for two different tasks, merge them, make one FIFO, and then time multiplex the two functions over one FIFO," Diamantidis explained.Cognichip claims that ACI can estimate not only the immediate PPA consequences of such changes but also their potential impact on physical implementation."These trade-offs become visible now because we can tell the designer essentially in real time what some of these impacts are going to be to downstream parasitics and downstream congestion and all those kinds of effects."The general idea behind ACI is to resolve potential architectural problems before RTL reaches physical design engineers rather than wait for implementation results and revise the architecture afterward."Our expectation is that there will be no loopbacks to the designer in terms of 'let us do this again because we did not meet this goal or because we ran into congestion issues,'" said Diamantidis.However, the accuracy of these predictions is critical. Cognichip claims its models can predict certain PPA characteristics with errors of approximately 10% relative to results obtained from conventional EDA tools at the pre-route stage of physical implementation.Cognichip evaluated its technology using 1,200 open-source designs and compared its predictions with those produced by general-purpose AI models, including Anthropic's Claude Opus and Google's Gemini. According to him, general-purpose models produced errors of approximately 50% – 100%, depending on the metric, whereas Cognichip's models reduced prediction errors to around 10%."[General purpose models] do not do well when it comes to predicting delays," Diamantidis said. "So, we take that down to within 10%. Again, 10% because think about it, we are running it at RTL. We do not have much physical information at all, right?"There is an important distinction, though. Cognichip's reported accuracy refers to pre-route physical implementation results, not final post-route characteristics. Actual routing introduces interconnect and power delivery parasitics as well as other physical effects that can alter timing and power consumption. Consequently, the reported 10% prediction error does not necessarily mean that ACI-generated designs will achieve their estimated PPA targets after physical implementation and signoff.Another question concerns the range of architectures and manufacturing technologies for which ACI can deliver such accuracy. Although Cognichip says its models incorporate semiconductor physics and account for process-dependent characteristics, it has not disclosed which foundry nodes it supports or how prediction accuracy varies across them.Diamantidis explained that some architectural decisions are largely independent of manufacturing technology, whereas others become increasingly dependent on the target process node as development progresses."[Think about chip development as a tree], at the top of the tree, there are decisions that are not really foundry-specific; they are closer to microarchitecture," he explained. "Then, of course, as you start working your way down the tree, at some point you branch off because the decision may be targeted towards the TSMC node A versus TSMC node B, which will result in different prediction things. But there is a big trunk of decisions that are not really related to the node and are more related to the architecture and the way that the architecture is implemented. What we try to do is we try to think of this whole tree and provide a lot of feedback to designers, especially in a node-agnostic mode, and then, of course, at some point we have to become more node-aware."This distinction is exceedingly important for complex CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators, where physical constraints tend to have substantial impact on architectural decisions. Meanwhile, Cognichip does not claim that ACI must develop such processors as monolithic designs. Instead, the company says its technology can work with individual IP blocks and subsystems, which engineers can subsequently integrate into larger chips. Of course, integration of these individually optimized IP blocks into larger chips is a challenge.Big chip? Not a problem, but there is a caveatAlthough Cognichip says ACI can handle subsystems containing millions of logic gates (i.e., circuits that implement Boolean functions), combining multiple such designs into a complex SoC introduces additional constraints related to interconnect delays, clock distribution, shared memory bandwidth, power delivery, and floorplanning. Consequently, an architecture that achieves Pareto-optimal PPA characteristics as a standalone subsystem may no longer be optimal once integrated into a larger chip. According to Cognichip, ACI can account for these system-level interactions by aligning and optimizing individual blocks against global SoC and subsystem constraints.“Yes, ACI can align and optimize individual blocks to global SoC and subsystem constraints. It can be applied to both flat and hierarchical optimization problems,” Diamanditis said. (Image credit: Cognichip)Cognichip is not proposing a fundamentally new SoC development methodology, but rather automating substantial portions of conventional front-end workflows. Its ACI platform supports both flat and hierarchical optimization and can drive the partitioning and propagation of design constraints from the top level to individual blocks. According to Cognichip, ACI can decompose system-level constraints into requirements for individual components and then re-aggregate them as the blocks are integrated.“ACI does not require a flat design methodology; it can drive hierarchical design from the top or subsystem-top down, ensuring that constraints are decomposed going into components but then re-aggregated when blocks are integrated,” Diamanditis explained.According to Cognichip, ACI can handle individual IP blocks and subsystems containing millions of logic gates, which can subsequently be combined hierarchically into larger SoCs. The company emphasizes that the complexity of individual partitions, rather than their size, determines how effectively ACI can handle them. However, it remains to be seen how effectively ACI can coordinate architectural decisions and optimize PPA across an entire complex SoC in practice. After all, a Pareto-optimal CPU core, memory controller, and interconnect do not necessarily form a Pareto-optimal SoC, as their interactions introduce additional timing, bandwidth, power, and physical constraints.Then again, developers of complex SoCs already address these challenges with hierarchical design methodologies, system-level optimization, and integration, so ACI’s focus on individual subsystems does not necessarily represent a significant limitation.Feedback loops? No need for them!One of the questions that normally occurs when we talk about a tool that is only aimed at the front end of chip development is how it can handle feedback loops from physical implementation (more on this later). Such feedback loops occur when placement and routing reveal problems with timing, power consumption, die area, or routing congestion that cannot be resolved through physical design optimizations alone. In more serious cases, engineers must revise RTL, pipelines, memory hierarchies, or other architectural elements, which requires another round of functional verification, synthesis, and physical implementation. These iterations can take plenty of time and involve multiple engineering teams, which makes them particularly expensive. (Image credit: Cognichip)Cognichip says ACI can use physical implementation results to revise RTL and microarchitecture if necessary, although this is not the company's primary focus. Instead, it aims to prevent costly iterations between front-end and back-end design teams by predicting potential problems before physical implementation begins."We are still focused very much on what we can do in the front end to prevent these situations rather than fix them."If physical implementation reveals problems that require changes to RTL or microarchitecture, engineers can return to ACI with the relevant feedback (Cognichip does not specify with which file format that feedback must be submitted) and use the platform to revise their designs. Yet, ACI cannot resolve issues that require changes to the physical implementation itself, such as clock-tree synthesis or placement and routing."They can come back to our environments to provide additional guidance, additional prompting, additional information," Diamantidis said. "Then based on that information, we can of course perform an adaptation of the design […] if the issue can be addressed in the design itself, then of course we can do that."Since feedback loops are expensive, yet necessary parts of semiconductor chip development flow, I had to ask that question explicitly, and the answer was that there would be no need for feedback loops with ACI. As the question and response require a lot of minutiae, we've added them in full below.Anton Shilov: Can ACI ingest physical implementation reports from Cadence, Synopsys, or Siemens EDA tools, identify architectural bottlenecks, revise the microarchitecture, and RTL, and repeat the process until the design meets its PPA targets?Stelios Diamantidis: Actually, this is where we depart from conventional approaches. We do not need to wait until physical implementation to identify these issues. We have trained models with full physical-stack visibility, which enables them to predict PPA during the front-end design phase.For example, suppose you have one design that operates at a certain frequency and consumes a certain amount of power, and another that runs perhaps 20% slower but consumes significantly less power. We can identify these trade-offs before physical implementation.Ultimately, the changes you want to make involve RTL and design constraints. Traditionally, engineers develop the RTL and constraints and hand them over to the physical implementation team. That team implements the design and reports the results. If the design fails to meet its targets, the front-end team must make changes, and the process starts again.These iterations are very expensive in terms of time because they cross design boundaries and involve tools with long runtimes.By training our models on the full physical stack, we can now provide immediate feedback to front-end designers. For example, we might tell an engineer: 'If you want to reduce power consumption at the cost of 10% of your frequency, take two FIFOs that serve different functions, combine them into one, and time-multiplex the two functions over that FIFO.'That is just one example of a microarchitectural decision. We can make these trade-offs visible to designers in essentially real time because our models can predict their impact on downstream parasitics, routing congestion, and other physical characteristics.As a result, engineers can make these decisions in a closed loop during front-end development. Once they have resolved the microarchitectural trade-offs and produced well-structured RTL, they can hand the design over to the physical implementation team. Of course, the design still has to go through physical implementation tools.Our expectation is that there will be no need to return the design to the front-end team because it failed to meet its targets or encountered congestion problems. That is the fundamental change we aim to bring to the transition between front-end and back-end chip development.Third Party IP? No problemModern SoCs typically combine proprietary logic with third-party IP, including processor cores, memory controllers, interface IP, and other reusable components. However, developers do not necessarily have access to the RTL of licensed IP blocks, and licensing agreements may restrict how such information can be used. This raises the question of how ACI can integrate third-party IP without access to its internal implementation. (Image credit: Cognichip)According to Cognichip, this is not a problem. ACI does not need to examine proprietary RTL to integrate an existing IP block into a larger design. Such IPs provide relevant interface specifications, including pin connections, signals, and their characteristics. ACI can then proceed with necessary integration logic and connect the IP to other subsystems."Most people want to take […] third-party licensed IP and optimize the integration of the IP," claims Diamantidis. "We ourselves do not ingest the guts of the IPs, nor do we try to train on any kind of data related to the IPs."The CPO of Cognichip stressed that ACI Enterprise protects customers' IP within the company's firewalled data centers and prevents it from entering third-party AI training pipelines. The platform provides customer-controlled access to sensitive information, multi-tenant isolation, and security controls validated through a SOC 2 Type II examination. However, these protections do not supersede the licensing restrictions imposed by third-party IP providers.A new offering Cognichip's ACI technology could substantially improve chip development productivity by automating labor-intensive tasks such as architectural exploration, RTL development, verification, and PPA optimization. (Image credit: Cognichip)The company's benchmark with a major chip designer suggests that the potential gains could be considerable, although the complexity of the project remains undisclosed. Such capabilities could be particularly valuable for startups and newcomers to the semiconductor industry, which tend to lack engineering resources and extensive IP portfolios of established chipmakers. By reducing the time, costs, and expertise required to develop custom silicon, ACI could lower the barriers to entry and enable smaller companies to pursue a custom silicon strategy that would otherwise be prohibitively expensive.However, Cognichip has yet to demonstrate autonomous development of a complete, physically validated chip, let alone a sophisticated CPU or GPU. The company does not perform physical implementation, and its expectations of eliminating costly feedback loops depend on the accuracy of its PPA predictions. It also remains to be seen how effectively ACI can optimize complex SoCs that combine numerous proprietary and third-party IP blocks under common power, performance, and area constraints.Ultimately, the Cognichip technology's value for leading-edge chip developers will depend not only on how quickly it can produce verified RTL, but also on how closely its predictions match the results of physical implementation and how much engineering work it can eliminate across the entire development cycle.
